subject: ENME
title: Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering Block Course
description: Special topics in Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering. Research and industry presentations, software training, informational sessions, and field trips as resources permit.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (32 HOURS), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: ENME
title: Mechanics of  Solids I
description: Review of axial-force, shear-force, bending moment and torque diagrams. Review of vector and matrix algebra. Kinematics of deformation and strain. Concept of stress. Constitutive equations. The states of plane stress and plane strain. Solutions to elementary elasticity problems -- axial force, torsion, bending, shear force. Deflection of beams. Euler buckling. Yield criteria.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-1.5T-3/2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Engineering Materials
description: Materials science, with an emphasis on the structure of materials and processing-structure property relationships, including atomic models, equilibrium phase diagrams, kinetics and non-equilibrium transformation diagrams, thermo-mechanical processing, microstructure formation and control, strengthening mechanisms, material selection, and an introduction to fracture.
prerequisites_raw: Engineering 204.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-1T-3/2)

subject: ENME
title: Computing Tools for Engineering Design
description: The application of computer tools to solve practical engineering problems; engineering computing including algorithm development, debugging, and verification and interpretation of results; mathematical modelling using high level programming languages and fundamentals of numerical analysis; to data analysis using machine learning concepts.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-2)

subject: ENME
title: Engineering Graphics and CAD
description: Technical sketching. Orthographic projections. Multiviews, auxiliary views and section views. Dimensions and tolerances. Working drawings. Design applications. Computer-Aided Design (CAD) software is used for 3D modelling and 2D drawing.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Fundamentals of Fluid Mechanics
description: Basic principles of mechanics of fluids. Fluid statics: forces on surfaces, buoyancy, stability. Continuity, energy and momentum equations applied to control-volume analysis. Dimensional analysis and physical similarity. Introduction to external flows and flow through pipes. Applications to a variety of problems in mechanical engineering.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-1.5T-2/2)

subject: ENME
title: Materials Selection in Engineering Design
description: Design-led course introducing a systematic methodology for selecting materials, manufacturing processes, and structural shapes during engineering design processes. Topics include materials property charts, materials selection basics and case studies, processes and their effect on properties, process selection and cost, multiple constraints and conflicting objectives, and materials and the environment.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-3/2)

subject: ENME
title: Mechatronics, Measurement, and Instrumentation
description: Components of measurement systems. Dynamic modelling of mechatronic systems and their transient and frequency response. Conversion of sensor outputs to voltage. Signal conditioning, amplifiers, and filters. Statistical analysis of measurement uncertainty. Digitization, sampling, aliasing, noise, and quantization error. Operating principles of sensors and actuators and their selection for industrial measurement and control.
prerequisites_raw: Engineering 225, 349, and Mathematics 375, and 3 units from Digital Engineering 319, Engineering 319, or Electrical Engineering 419.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-1T-3/2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Heat Transfer
description: Modes of heat transfer; conduction, convection, radiation. Conduction in plane walls and cylinders. Conduction-convection systems, fins. Principles of convection. Empirical and practical relations for forced convection heat transfer. Natural convection. Condensation and boiling heat transfer. Heat exchangers. The log-mean temperature difference method.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-1T-2/2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Fundamentals of Kinematics and Dynamics Of Machines
description: Basic mechanisms and linkages in machinery. Kinematics and kinetics of mechanisms. Cam design and dynamic analysis. Ordinary and planetary gear trains.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-1T), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Mechanics of Solids II
description: One-dimensional viscoelasticity. Review of Linear Algebra. Kinematics of the deformation, strain and compatibility. Balance equations, stress and equilibrium. Linear elastic constitutive equations. Initial and boundary conditions in linear elasticity. Solution to axi-symmetric and two-dimensional boundary value problems in elasticity. Failure criteria. Principle of virtual work and energy methods. The stiffness, Rayleigh-Ritz and finite element numerical methods in solid mechanics.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-1.5T-2/2)

subject: ENME
title: Mechanical Engineering Thermodynamics
description: Review of fundamentals; thermodynamic properties; flow and non-flow processes; Carnot cycle; Rankine cycle including reheat and regeneration. Engine gas cycles including Otto, Diesel and dual combustion cycles; simple gas turbines; reheat, intercooling, and heat exchange. Reciprocating air compressors and expanders. Heat-pump and refrigeration cycles and their performance criteria. Air conditioning process and psychrometry. Combustion processes, chemical equilibrium, dissociation.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-1T-3/2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Machine Component Design
description: Introduction to the principles of machine component design. Design for stiffness, strength, and endurance. Surface contacts, wear, and lubrication. Tolerances and fits. Design and selection of mechanical elements such as shafts, bolted joints, welded joints, hydrodynamic bearings, ball and roller bearings, gears, belts, brakes, clutches, and springs.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-2T), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Fluid Mechanics
description: Control volume methodology for multi-dimensional systems as applied to conservation principles (mass, linear and angular momentum); Navier-Stokes equations applied to pipe and boundary layer flows; basic principles of potential flow theory and aerodynamics and an introduction to compressible flow (convergent-divergent channels and normal shocks).
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-1.5T-2/2)

subject: ENME
title: Mechanical Engineering Capstone Design Project I
description: A team-based project course with the focus on the design process associated with mechanical and manufacturing engineering. The design process consists of the stages of conceptual design, design development and verification. Project management, teamwork and communication are emphasized for professional development.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (0-4), WIL Field Placement, Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: ENME
title: Mechanical Engineering Capstone Design Project II
description: A continuation of the capstone design project, where student teams build on their design work in Part I.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (0-4), WIL Field Placement, Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: ENME
title: Robotics
description: Kinematics, statics, dynamics and control of robot arms. Robot actuators, drives, sensors, and vision. Applications of robots.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-3/2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
description: Advanced topics in Mechanical Engineering.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Materials Characterization Techniques
description: Techniques for materials and mechanical characterization relevant to research and industrial applications. Topics include, but are not limited to, fatigue, creep, nanoindentation (and wear), elements of crystallography, X-ray diffraction, the principle of electron microscopy, and advanced analytical tools.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-2/2)

subject: ENME
title: Digital Logic and Control
description: Logic gates and digital circuits; Boolean algebra; sequential logic; finite state machines; ladder logic and PLC programming; stability and response of discrete-time systems; the z-transform; digital feedback design via root locus; applications of digital logic and control.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-1T)

subject: ENME
title: Finite Element Method
description: One- and multi-dimensional problems in linear and steady heat conduction and elasticity. Emphasis on: strong and weak formulation of the boundary value problems (BVP) and their approximation by Galerkin's method; fundamentals of finite element interpolation and construction of interpolation functions for a variety of multi-dimensional element shapes; existence and uniqueness of the solution; error estimates; finite element arrays and data structures employed in computer programs; numerical integration techniques; and mesh construction.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-2)

subject: ENME
title: Physical Metallurgy
description: Various aspects of physical metallurgy. Topics include basic crystallography, phase diagrams and alloy theory, dislocation theory, point defects, diffusion, plastic deformation and dislocation behavior, surfaces, grain boundaries, and interfaces, work hardening and annealing, steel and steel transformations, and precipitation hardening. The concepts of alloy design and the physical basis that links the structure of materials with their properties will be introduced.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Mechatronics Design Laboratory I
description: A hands-on laboratory experience in the design and analysis of electro-mechanical components. Introduction to microprocessor-controlled electromechanical systems. Laboratory projects to configure, design, and implement a succession of mechatronic systems. Topics of lectures and labs include aliasing, quantization, electronic feedback, power amplifiers, digital logic, encoder interfacing, and motor control.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (1-4), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: ENME
title: Mechatronics Design Laboratory II
description: More sophisticated and in-depth topics in mechatronic systems design explored through laboratory exercises, and complemented by selected lecture topics including practical control aspects of saturation and tuning and machine learning introduction.
prerequisites_raw: Mechanical Engineering 561; and Mechanical Engineering 585 or Electrical Engineering 441
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (1-4), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: ENME
title: Aerodynamics
description: An introductory course in aerodynamics for engineers. Kinematics and dynamics of viscous and inviscid flow; airfoil dynamics including thin airfoil theory and lifting line theory, finite wings, panel methods and airfoil parameters. Boundary layer theory and boundary layer control as applied in aerodynamics. Introduction to computational fluid dynamics and experimental aerodynamics.
prerequisites_raw: Mechanical Engineering 495.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-2/2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Aeroelasticity
description: Introduction to the interactions between structural dynamics (elastic and inertia forces) and aerodynamic forces. Students will learn the main concepts of static aeroelasticity (lift distribution, divergence and control effectiveness) and dynamic aeroelasticity (flutter) for fixed-wing aircraft. Students will learn how to derive the equations of motion for complete aeroelastic systems, apply various methods of structural dynamics analysis and perform simplified analysis of static and dynamic aeroelastic phenomena. Students will also learn the elementary methods of incorporating aeroelastic phenomena in aircraft design and the importance of doing so from a practical point of view. The main objective of this course is to provide students with the technical background to understand the main principles of aircraft aeroelasticity.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-1T), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
description: An introduction to finite volume and finite element approximations; turbulence modelling, including Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS), Large Eddy Simulation (LES), and Variational Multi-Scale (VMS) methods; time-marching schemes; linear and non-linear solvers; grid generation and adaptation; post-processing of the solution; and parallel computing (with the focus on MPI).
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-2)

subject: ENME
title: Design of Lightweight Structures
description: Overview of high-performance lightweight design strategies used in structural applications, with focus on fibre-reinforced polymer composites. Composite mechanics; buckling; introduction to topological optimization; considerations for material selection and manufacturing, characterization, and testing.  Applications to aerospace design will be discussed. Practical skills to be developed through a laboratory component.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-3/2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Propulsion
description: Introduction to propulsion for aerospace vehicles. Air-breathing and rocket propulsion systems analyzed using principles from thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, and combustion. Individual components such as intakes, compressors, combustors, heat exchangers, turbines, and nozzles will be introduced. Performance parameters, such as thermal and propulsive efficiencies, specific fuel consumption, thrust-to-weight ratio, specific impulse, total impulse, and characteristic velocity, will be used to assess various propulsion concepts.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-1T-3/2)

subject: ENME
title: Building Energy Modelling and Simulation
description: Fundamentals of heating, ventilating, and air conditioning systems in buildings. Psychrometrics. Indoor environmental quality. Climatic design information. Heating and cooling loads. Air distribution systems control. Codes, regulations, and standards. Application of building energy simulation software. Design of mechanical systems for small building.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: ENME
title: Control Systems
description: Modelling and dynamic response of physical systems; feedback control; stability; performance specification in the time and frequency domains; root locus plots; Bode and Nyquist plots; Proportional/Integral/Derivative (PID) control and dynamic compensation.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-1T-3/2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Continuum Mechanics
description: Kinematics of deformation, concept of stress, balance of mass, linear momentum, angular momentum and energy. Thermodynamics of continua. Constitutive equations for viscous fluids and nonlinear elastic solids.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Gas Dynamics
description: Fundamentals of one-dimensional gas dynamics. Isentropic and non-isentropic flows, applications of dynamical similarity to shock waves. Oblique shocks, supersonic nozzles, flows with friction or heat transfer. Introduction to computational fluid dynamics (CFD).
prerequisites_raw: Mechanical Engineering 495.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-1T-2/2)

subject: ENME
title: Turbomachinery
description: Performance of turbomachines, machine selection, Reynolds number and scale effects. Two dimensional flow in turbomachines, degree of reaction and vector diagrams; flow irreversibilities and loss coefficients; pump, compressor and turbine efficiencies. Design of pumps, fans, centrifugal compressors, axial-flow compressors, and axial-flow turbines. Combination of machines with pipes or ducts.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-1T-3/2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Vibrations and Machine Dynamics
description: Linear vibration theory: free and forced vibration of single- and multi- degree-of-freedom systems; damping in machines; vibration absorbers; experimental modal analysis. Balance of rotating machinery: sources of unbalance, rigid rotors, flexible rotors, critical speeds, balancing principles. Lagrange equations: application to mechanical systems.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-1T-3/2)

subject: ENME
title: Introduction to Numerical Methods for Engineers
description: Introduction to mathematical modelling, sources of errors in the process of numerical analysis and solution methodology; Elements of numerical analysis, Taylor series, round-off error, truncation error, concept of stability, consistency and convergence; Linear algebra, Matrices, normal forms, Gauss elimination method, LU-decomposition, tridiagonal systems of equations; iterative methods, Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel, SOR, SSOR methods, finite difference and finite control volume concepts and stability analysis; Parabolic equations: explicit and implicit methods, time-splitting method.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Advanced Robotics
description: Review of kinematics and dynamics of serial-link manipulators and the Euler-Lagrange method. Kinematics and dynamics of parallel manipulators. Position, force, and impedance control of manipulators. Whole-body control. Advanced path and trajectory planning. Redundant manipulators and trajectory optimization.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Physical Fluid Dynamics
description: Physical phenomena of incompressible fluid motion for a variety of flows, e.g. pipe and channel flow, flow past a cylinder, and convection in horizontal layers. The derivation of the basic equations of fluid mechanics using Cartesian tensor notation. High and low Reynolds number flows including some solutions of the viscous flow equations, inviscid flow, and elementary boundary layer theory. Thermal free convective flows.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Combustion Processes
description: Review of thermodynamics and chemical kinetics of combustion. Fluid mechanics, heat and mass transfer in combustion phenomena. Autoignition and source ignition, flames and detonation. Quenching and explosion hazards, flammability and detonation limits. Heterogeneous combustion, combustion practical systems, combustion as affecting pollution and efficiency, some experimental combustion methods.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Advanced Thermodynamics
description:
Basic relations and the first law; the second law of thermodynamics; availability and exergy analysis; availability and exergy analysis of cycles; finite time thermodynamics; equations of state; thermodynamic property relations; thermodynamic properties of homogeneous mixtures; multiphase-multicomponent systems; chemically reacting systems; special topics: entropy generation minimization, pinch technology, thermodynamics and decarbonization.

Also known as: (formerly ENME 619.37 Advanced Thermodynamics)
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Mechanics Of Compressible Flow
description: One-dimensional steady and unsteady motion with application to the analysis of supersonic nozzles, diffusers, flow in conduits with Friction, shock tubes. Two-dimensional flow of ideal fluid. Small perturbation theory, method of characteristics with application to design of supersonic nozzles. Waves in two-dimensional flow.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Research Seminar I
description:
Students will develop written and oral communication skills required to disseminate their technical research results and to receive formative feedback on performance.

NOT INCLUDED IN GPA
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3S-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Reliability Engineering
description: Theory and practical implementation of statistics in reliability; Mean time to failure; Availability; Reliability block diagrams; Root cause analysis; Load-strength interference; First-order reliability methods; Time to failure for selected failure mechanisms; System reliability model; Machine learning for reliability engineering and safety.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Sensors, Data and Signal Analysis
description: Basic principles relating to measurement systems. Static and dynamic characteristics of signals. Measurement system behaviour. Application of probability and statistics to measurement systems. Uncertainty analysis. Data acquisition and conversion, analog/digital signals and associated sampling theory. Application of theory to various measurement systems such as pressure, velocity, strain, concentration, and temperature.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-3/2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Environmental Fluid Mechanics
description: Overview of fluid mechanics fundamentals; Boundary layer theory; Turbulence theory; Turbulent structures; Simulation of environmental flow and transportation of air pollutants; Dynamics of particulates dispersed in gases; Environmental applications (Two-phase flow and particulate removal; Turbulence and dispersion in low atmosphere).
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Uncertainty Quantification and Scientific Machine Learning
description: An introduction to predictive modeling and uncertainty quantification for scientific and engineering applications. Key concepts include: Bayesian interference, stochastic differential equations, Monte Carlo methods for uncertainty propagation; supervised learning techniques including Bayesian regression, Gaussian processes, and deep learning; unsupervised methods; state space models with applications such as mechanical vibrations. A hands-on approach to data science and machine learning is emphasized over theoretical derivations.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Special Problems
description:
Designed to provide graduate students, especially at the PhD level, with the opportunity of pursuing advanced studies in particular areas under the direction of a faculty member. Students would be required to consider problems of an advanced nature.

MAY BE REPEATED FOR CREDIT
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Pump and Compressor Stations
description: Basic role of pump and compressor stations on a pipeline. Design and performance of centrifugal, screw and reciprocating compressors and centrifugal and positive displacement pumps. Design and performance of drivers including gas turbines, engines and electric motors. Design and functions of auxiliary systems, including bearings and lubrication systems, seals and sealing systems and instrumentation and controls. Design studies for acoustic/mechanical and torsional analysis. Pump and compression station equipment and functions.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Fundamentals of Pipeline Economics
description: Provides students with a fundamental understanding of engineering economics, including decision-making processes and life-cycle assessment in application to pipeline systems.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Corrosion Science in the Pipelines Industry
description: Overview of corrosion in the pipeline industry with emphasis on the underlying science, including thermodynamics and kinetics of electrochemical processes, corrosion prevention and mitigation by materials selection, inhibition, coatings and cathodic protection. Implications for integrity management will also be discussed.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Pipeline Coatings
description: Introduction to the fundamental properties and structure of coatings, as well as applications in the pipeline industry. Applications of coating technology in integrity maintenance of the various structural facilities. Computer assisted coatings project management programs will be introduced.
antirequisites_raw: Credit for Mechanical Engineering 628 and 619.27 (Pipeline Coatings) will not be allowed
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Fundamentals of Liquid Hydraulics in Pipeline Systems
description: Introduction to the fundamentals of liquid hydraulics in pipeline systems. Topics include petroleum fluids, design elements and economics, mechanical design, fluid mechanics fundamentals, pipeline hydraulics, isothermal flow, pumping requirements, centrifugal and reciprocating pumps, operations and maintenance design, and design optimization.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Advanced Numerical Methods For Engineers
description: Introduction, mathematical modelling, sources of errors in the process of numerical analysis and solution methodology; Elements of numerical analysis, Taylor series, round-off error, truncation error, concept of stability, consistency and convergence; Linear algebra, normal forms, Gauss elimination method, LU-decomposition, tridiagonal systems of equations; iterative methods, Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel, SOR, SSOR methods, conjugate gradient methods and preconditioning and principles of the multi-grid methods; Elliptic "equilibrium" equation, Laplace and Poisson equations, finite difference and finite control volume concepts and stability analysis; Parabolic equations: explicit, implicit and Crank-Nicolson methods, time-splitting method, method of lines, Stability analysis; Hyperbolic equations; Introduction to other methods; future challenging problems.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Fundamentals of Gas Hydraulics in Pipeline Systems
description: Applications of fundamental fluid mechanics concepts to pipelines conveying compressible media (gases). Strategies for describing the gas-dynamics of pipeline systems and networks are developed, as well as the influence of gas properties and pipeline operating characteristics on component selection and operating parameters.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Mathematical Techn For Engineers
description: Application of mathematical techniques to the solution of ordinary and partial differential equations arising in engineering problems. Methods that will be considered are: separation of variables, method of characteristics, transform methods and complex variable methods. Methods for analysis and solution of algebraic equations, including Riccati equations and Diophantine equations.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Pipeline Geotechnical Engineering
description: Introduction to applications of geotechnical engineering in design and construction of oil and gas pipelines. Geohazard assessment and mitigation methods and issues around pipe/soil interaction will be discussed, as well as the relevant codes, standards and industry guidelines for pipelines.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Structural Analysis of Buried Steel Pipeline Systems
description: An introduction to stress analysis of buried pipelines through hand calculations, spreadsheets, and stress analysis software. Pipeline code requirements are discussed. Individual practices and industry examples are used.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Thermal Systems Analysis
description: Fundamentals of thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer and combustion; Modelling of thermophysical properties; Second law of thermodynamics, concept of entropy generation and exergy analysis; Minimizing environmental impact; Advanced design and analysis of heat exchangers, co-generation, renewable energy systems, and propulsion systems.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Numerical Methods for Computational Fluid Dynamics
description: Review of solution techniques for ordinary differential equations. Stability, consistency and convergence. Order of accuracy. Fourier methods for stability. Numerical techniques for one,- two- and three-dimensional linear parabolic problems. Courant condition. Implicit and semi-implicit schemes. Boundary conditions for parabolic problems. Techniques for linear hyperbolic problems. CFL condition. Characteristics, domain of dependence and domain of influence. Boundary conditions for hyperbolic problems. Nonlinear conservation laws. The Burger's equation as a test problem. Strong and weak solutions. Conservative and integral forms. Conservative schemes. Entropy condition. Godunov theorem and flux limiters. Godunov, ENO and TVD schemes. Implementation in gas dynamics.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Stress Corrosion Cracking of Materials
description: Fundamentals of stress corrosion cracking (SCC) of materials and the factors contributing to SCC from environmental, metallurgical and mechanical sources. Various testing techniques to study and/or evaluate SCC will also be discussed.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Advanced Control Systems
description: Introduction to multivariable systems; state space models; analysis of linear systems; stability; Cayley-Hamilton theorem; controllability and observability; state feedback control; pole placement designs; introduction to linear optimal control and estimation; Kalman filtering; separation theorem and duality; performance specifications; loop transfer recovery; introduction to infinity norm methods.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Construction & Project Management
description: Construction sequences for large pipe; clearing, grading, trenching, stringing; techniques for smaller pipe and narrower right of way; joining of HDPE; right of way; salvage, automatic welding; ultrasonic and radiographic inspection; record keeping; as built drawings and alignment sheets; hydrostatic testing; purging and commissioning; ground bed installation; cathodic protection.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -G, GFC Hours (12 HOURS)

subject: ENME
title: Optimal and Adaptive Control
description: Studies of leading-edge and emerging control theory and technology; direct adaptive control, system identification using least-squares analysis; self-tuning control; indirect adaptive control; model reference adaptive control; sliding mode control in continuous and discrete time; optimal design of sliding mode controllers; optimal control design using various and multiple norms; implementation of robust controllers; robust stability and robust performance objectives.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Welding & Joining Processes
description: Welding and joining methods and inspection techniques. Some of welding includes fusion welding (e.g., MIG, TIG, stick welding, SAW) and non-fusion welding (e.g., friction welding). Other joining methods, such as soldering, brazing, adhesives, fasteners, and interference fits. Quality control and inspection techniques for welding (NDE).
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -G, GFC Hours (12 HOURS)

subject: ENME
title: Finite Element for Engineers
description: Introduction to a Finite Element Method (FEM). Focus will be on one- and two-dimensional, steady-state problems in linear elasticity and heat conduction. The focus would be on numerical approach to solve boundary value problems (BVP) using Galerkin's method; mesh generation; postprocessing of the solution; usage of the commercial tools to solve physical problems using FEM.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Finite Element Method
description: One- and multi-dimensional problems in linear and steady heat conduction and elasticity. Emphasis on: strong and weak formulation of the boundary value problems (BVP) and their approximation by Galerkin's method; fundamentals of finite element interpolation and construction of interpolation functions for a variety of multi-dimensional element shapes; existence and uniqueness of the solution; error estimates; finite element arrays and data structures employed in computer programs; numerical integration techniques; and mesh construction.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Mobile Robotics
description: Overview of unmanned vehicles, mobile robot locomotion systems, wheeled rovers, walking machines, mobile-manipulators, mobile robot sensors and actuators, simulation, modelling and analysis of mobile robot behaviour, robot-environment interaction analysis, 2D navigation techniques and localization, mobile robot simulation tools.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Advanced Continuum Mechanics
description: Review of linear algebra: vector spaces, linear maps, tensors; affine spaces: coordinate systems and differential calculus; kinematics of continua: deformation and strain tensors, deformation and strain rates; balance equations: mass, linear momentum, angular momentum, energy; entropy inequality; stress tensors; stress rates; stress power and conjugated stress-strain pairs; constitutive theory: constitutive axioms, hyperelastic solids, perfect and Newtonian fluids.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Propulsion
description: Introduction to propulsion for aerospace vehicles. Air-breathing and rocket propulsion systems analyzed using principles from thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, and combustion. Individual components such as intakes, compressors, combustors, heat exchangers, turbines, and nozzles will be introduced. Performance parameters, such as thermal and propulsive efficiencies, specific fuel consumption, thrust-to-weight ratio, specific impulse, total impulse, characteristic velocity will be used to assess various propulsion concepts.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-1T-3/2)

subject: ENME
title: Physical Metallurgy
description:
Various aspects of physical metallurgy including basic crystallography; phase diagrams and alloy theory; dislocation theory; point defects; diffusion; plastic deformation and dislocation behavior; surfaces, grain boundaries, and interfaces; work hardening and annealing; steel and steel transformations; and precipitation hardening. The concepts of alloy design and the physical basis that links the structure of materials with their properties will be introduced.

Also known as: (formerly Mechanical Engineering 619.82 Physical Metallurgy)
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Mechatronics Design Laboratory I
description: A hands-on laboratory experience in the design and analysis of electro-mechanical components. Introduction to microprocessor-controlled electromechanical systems. Laboratory projects to configure, design, and implement a succession of mechatronic systems. Topics of lectures and labs include aliasing, quantization, electronic feedback, power amplifiers, digital logic, encoder interfacing, and motor control.
antirequisites_raw: Credit for Mechanical Engineering 661 and any of 560, 561, 619.47 (Advanced Mechatronics I) or 660 will not be allowed.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (1-4), Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related, Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Mechatronics Design Laboratory II
description: Continuation of Mechanical Engineering 661, involving more sophisticated and in-depth topics in mechatronic systems design explored through laboratory exercises, and complemented by selected lecture topics including practical control aspects of saturation and tuning and machine learning introduction.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (1-4), Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related, Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: (KNES/MDSC 663) Advanced Muscle Mechanics and Physiology
description: A look at problems associated within muscle mechanics and contractility. Also the use of muscle mechanics as a scientific discipline to critically learn and evaluate the scientific process. Basic anatomy and physiology of muscle contraction including the cross-bridge theory, and the force-length, force-velocity and force-time relationships of actively and passively contracting muscles will also be covered.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Pipeline Design
description: Function and types of pipeline systems; gathering, transmission, distribution. Design parameters and procedures: supply and demand considerations; design life; capacity planning; system planning and facilities. Hydraulic design. Mechanical design. Geotechnical design.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -G, GFC Hours (12 HOURS)

subject: ENME
title: Advanced Materials Engineering
description: Covers a variety of material aspects and provides a fundamental understanding of Materials Science and Engineering. Emphasizes the understanding of advanced dislocation theory and its application in illustration of diffusion, deformation and fracture of metals. Fundamentals of material strengthening mechanisms are covered. Practical aspects that are relevant to material uses and failures, such as environmental-induced cracking, creep, fatigue, strain aging and corrosion, are discussed. Typical surface analysis techniques for material characterization are introduced.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Fracture Mechanics
description: Basic fracture theory, failure criteria, overview of fracture mechanics, brittle and ductile failure, crack tip parameters, geometric considerations, methods of analysis, fracture toughness and testing standards. Applications in design, fatigue subcritical crack growth, creep and impact.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Pipeline Economics
description: Macroeconomics of system supply and demand, open season procedures, optimized sizing, J curves; CAPEX, OPEX, taxation, leasing, depreciation and capital cost allowance, developing revenue requirement, cost of service. Salvage and end of life cost. For utilities Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC).
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -G, GFC Hours (12 HOURS)

subject: ENME
title: Fatigue of Materials
description: History and origin of fatigue. Stress life, strain life and fracture mechanics approaches. Low and high cycle fatigue. Low and high temperature fatigue. Combined stresses, initiation, and propagation of cracks. Environmental and statistical effects. Testing techniques and variables. Design and specific material behaviour. Mechanisms of fatigue.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENME
title: Aerodynamics
description: Kinematics and dynamics of viscous and inviscid flow; airfoil dynamics including thin airfoil theory and lifting line theory, finite wings, panel methods and airfoil parameters. Boundary layer theory and boundary layer control as applied in aerodynamics. Introduction to computational fluid dynamics and experimental aerodynamics.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-2/2)

subject: ENME
title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
description: Topics include: finite volume and finite element approximations; overview of turbulence models, including Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS), Large Eddy Simulation (LES), and Variational Multi-Scale (VMS); time-marching schemes; methods to solve system of linear equations (e.g. GMRES, Conjugate Gradient); grid generation and adaptation; and post-processing of the solution using VisIt and ParaView. Also includes an introduction to parallel computing.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Gas and Liquid Hydraulics
description: Properties of liquids and gases, steady-state, transient, multiphase, pressure drop due to friction, pressure required to transport, liquid pumping and gas compression, valves and flow measurement.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -G, GFC Hours (12 HOURS)

subject: ENME
title: Materials Selection and Metallurgy
description: Fundamentals of physical metallurgy of carbon steels. Principles of steel strengthening. Evolution of pipeline steels. Composition, microstructures and properties of low- and high-grade pipeline steels. Thermo-mechanical controlling processing of high-strength pipeline steels. Performance and failure of pipeline steels in service.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -G, GFC Hours (12 HOURS)

subject: ENME
title: Pipeline Stress Analysis
description: Introduction to the stress analysis and design of buried pipelines. Allowable working stress design and strain-based design. Considerations such as operating pressure/temperature, buoyancy, buckling, and pipe-soil interaction are examined. Pipeline flexibility analysis is explored using both analytical and numerical methods. Mitigation strategies for pipelines are discussed. The pertinent requirements of the current North American pipeline codes are addressed.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -G, GFC Hours (12 HOURS)

subject: ENME
title: Geotechnical Aspects in Pipeline Engineering
description: Soil types and classification, soil testing, soil strength-deformation determination, safe burial depth, ground movement in on-shore and offshore, loading pattern on pipelines, soil-pipe interaction and monitoring (in moving slopes, muskeg, permafrost, seabed, and river crossing), performance assessment of pipelines under different in situ environmental loading, ALA and PRCI design guidelines.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -G, GFC Hours (12 HOURS)

subject: ENME
title: Environmental Impact and Regulatory Matters
description: Examines pipelines as linear assets which cross a wide variety of ecosystems and communities; public concerns about health, safety, archeological and environmental protection, and participation of stakeholders with diverse interests, including First Nations; and the complexity of regulatory processes. Topics include environmental impact assessment, public consultation and roles and responsibility of regulators.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -G, GFC Hours (12 HOURS)

subject: ENME
title: Operation and Maintenance
description: Automation overview, SCADA systems, station control, instrumentation and metering, custody transfer, nominations process, scheduling and batching multi products. Recommended practices for land usage, ROW patrols, pipeline repair: protocols; repair methods; codes and standards; reference technical papers.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -G, GFC Hours (12 HOURS)

subject: ENME
title: Automation and Control Systems
description: The basics of industrial automation and control systems, with an emphasis on their application to the energy industry in the areas of safety and energy savings. The key technologies considered will be programmable logic controllers (PLC), supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems, and distributed control systems (DCS).
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -G, GFC Hours (12 HOURS)

subject: ENME
title: Applications of 3D Rigid Body Mechanics in Biomechanics
description: Applications of 3D motion analysis and rigid body mechanics to musculoskeletal system locomotion, and movement. Experimental, theoretical and numerical methods for optical motion imaging, 3D analysis of joint kinematics and kinetics, joint angle representations, prediction of joint forces, data analysis and filtering, error propagation, inverse and forward dynamics approaches, and applications to clinical and orthopaedic engineering.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Corrosion, Cracking, and Coatings
description: Electrochemical principles of corrosion reactions. Internal and external corrosion of buried pipelines. Principle of cathodic protection. Evolution of pipeline coating technology. Coating performance in conjunction with cathodic protection. Failure modes and effect analysis of pipeline coatings. Stress corrosion cracking of pipelines, along with corrosion fatigue and hydrogen-induced cracking of pipeline steels.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -G, GFC Hours (12 HOURS)

subject: ENME
title: (MDSC 685) Biomechanics of Human Movement
description: Introduction to the measuring methods (accelerometry, goniometry, film and film analysis, video systems) of biomechanical analysis of human movement (force and force distribution). Description of the mechanical properties of bone, tendon, ligaments, cartilage, muscles and soft tissues. The relation between structure and function of biomaterials. Introduction to descriptive analysis of human movement.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ENME
title: Integrity Management
description: Overview and implementation of the integrity management program, threat management, failure mode identification, baseline assessment plan, fitness-for-service assessment using direct assessment and condition monitoring such as inline inspections and pressure testing; defects; defect analysis; risk reduction approaches and corrective actions, upgrading.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -G, GFC Hours (12 HOURS)

subject: ENME
title: Pipeline In-Line Inspection Technologies
description: Traditional in-line inspection (ILI) methods, including ultrasonic, EMAT, and MFL, and non-traditional ILI methods, such as eddy current, INS, and acoustic. Non-piggable lines. Discrepancies between reported vs. actual defects and anomalies.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -G, GFC Hours (12 HOURS)

subject: ENME
title: Pipeline Leak Detection Technologies
description: Computational pipeline monitoring (CPM) methods and external leak detection techniques, such as fiber optic, acoustic, and polymeric composite sensors. The internal leak detection methods include volume balance, rate of changes, real time transient model (RTTM), and negative pressure.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -G, GFC Hours (12 HOURS)

subject: ENME
title: Design and Manufacturing of Lightweight Structures
description:
Overview of high-performance lightweight design strategies used in structural applications, with focus on fibre-reinforced polymer composites. Composite mechanics; buckling; introduction to topological optimization; Considerations for material selection and, manufacturing, characterization and testing. Applications to aerospace design will be discussed. Practical skills to be developed through a laboratory component.  

Also known as: (Mechanical Engineering 573).
course_attributes: GFC Hours (3-3), Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D

subject: ENME
title: Graduate Project
description: Individual project in the student's area of specialization under the guidance of the student's supervisor. A written proposal, one or more written progress reports, and a final written report are required. An oral presentation is required upon completion of the course.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (0-4), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: ENME
title: Vibration and Machine Dynamics
description: Linear vibration theory: free and forced vibration of single- and multi- degree-of-freedom systems; damping in machines; vibration absorbers; experimental modal analysis. Balance of rotating machinery: sources of unbalance, rigid rotors, flexible rotors, critical speeds, balancing principles. Lagrange equations: application to mechanical systems. Signal analysis: time and frequency domain. Introduction to statistical signal analysis. Vibration measurement and analysis for condition monitoring.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-1T-3/2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENME
title: Turbulence
description: Provides an overview of turbulence in incompressible flows of Newtonian fluids. Topics include: the nature of turbulence; classical methods of analysis (Reynolds-averaging, spectral representations); the concept of scales; a review of isotropic and homogeneous turbulence; the energy cascade and the role of vorticity in turbulence canonical flows: boundary layers, jets, wakes and mixing layers; modern views of turbulence including coherent motions and inter-scale energy transfer.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (4-0)

subject: ENME
title: Research Seminar II
description:
Students will develop written and oral communication skills required to disseminate their technical research results and to receive formative feedback on performance.

NOT INCLUDED IN GPA
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3S-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENMF
title: Manufacturing and Production Processes
description: The role and characterization of manufacturing technology within the manufacturing enterprise. Overview of deformation processes, joining processes, consolidation processes, material-removal processes, and material alteration processes. Process selection and planning.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-3), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENMF
title: Modelling & Simulation of Manufacturing Systems
description: General modelling of production systems. Spreadsheet modelling for capacity analysis.  Fundamentals of discrete-event simulation including: key concepts; simulation world views; the simulation study life cycle. Modelling and programming aspects of discrete-event simulation including: verification and validation; simulation animation; interfacing simulation software with other systems. Statistical aspects of discrete-event simulation including: random number and random variate generation; input process modelling; output analysis; variance reduction techniques. Applications of discrete-event simulation to the design and analysis of manufacturing systems.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: ENMF
title: Computer-Aided Design and Manufacturing
description: Hardware and software for computer-aided design and manufacturing (CAD/CAM) systems. Geometric modelling, transformation and visualization. Modelling of freeform curves and surfaces. Programming for computer numerically controlled (CNC) machining. Integration of CAD/CAM systems, applications in motion analysis, structure analysis, optimization, additive manufacturing, reverse engineering and virtual engineering.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENMF
title: Advanced Manufacturing Systems
description: Manufacturing strategy and competitive manufacturing. Queuing theory and its application to manufacturing systems analysis (including rapid modelling tools). Linear programming and its application to manufacturing systems problems. Scheduling problems in manufacturing. Supply chain modelling and integration. Enterprise resource planning systems.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: ENMF
title: Integrated Manufacturing Systems
description: Fundamentals of integrated and competitive manufacturing. Manufacturing and operations strategy. Topics in production and operations management including: production planning and control systems; inventory management systems; process analysis and improvement; quality management systems.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-2)

subject: ENMF
title: Experimental Design and Analysis
description: Introduction to statistical Design of Experiments (DOE) techniques for efficient data collection, analysis and interpretation. Hypothesis testing, Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), including blocking and nesting, in both full and fractional factorial designs to identify and control sources of variability. Applications of these techniques to optimize product and process performance through data-driven experimentation.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: ENMF
title: Project Engineering
description: The project lifecycle. Project planning, scheduling, and control. Resource considerations. Cost estimating, planning, and performance. Project risk. Project personnel and organizational structures.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-2/2)

subject: ENMF
title: Introduction to Microelectromechanical Systems
description: Microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) and devices including microsensors and microactuators. Principles of operation, material properties, fabrication techniques including surface and bulk micro­machining, IC-derived microfabrication techniques, sensing and actuation principles, sensor dynamics issues, circuit and system issues, packaging, calibration and testing. Illustrative examples include (1) micromachined inertial sensors and actuators for manufacturing processes, (2) microactuator arrays for "smart surfaces", (3) biosensors for medical applications, and (4) transducers for aerospace applications.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENMF
title: Manufacturing of Polymer Composites
description:
Overview of the considerations and challenges in processing fibre-reinforced polymer composites.  Introduction and discussion of constituent materials, reactive polymer composites, thermoplastic composites, textile preforms, autoclave processing, pultrusion, thermoforming, filament winding, liquid composite molding, process modelling, testing and characterization techniques.

Also known as: (formerly Manufacturing Engineering 619.03 (Manufact of Polymer Composites))
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - D, Fee Rate Group(International) -C, GFC Hours (3-3/2)

subject: ENMF
title: Advanced Robotics
description: Review of kinematics and dynamics of serial-link manipulators and the Euler-Lagrange method. Kinematics and dynamics of parallel manipulators. Position, force, and impedance control of manipulators. Lyapunov stability. Feedback linearization. Advanced path and trajectory planning. Redundant manipulators and trajectory optimization.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENMF
title: Plan & Control Comp Inte Manufact
description: Planning and Control of Computer Integrated Manufacturing Advanced techniques for the design, planning, and control of integrated manufacturing systems. Course elements include: a framework for manufacturing planning and control; data flow and structured modelling methodologies; hierarchical models of manufacturing; cellular manufacturing organization; databases and communications; forecasting, demand management, capacity planning and master production scheduling; materials requirements planning, manufacturing resource planning, Just-in-Time manufacture, and Optimized Production Technology; control of independent demand inventory items; production activity control, shop floor control, scheduling, order release and dispatching; simulation in planning and control.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENMF
title: Design and Analysis of Experiments
description: Statistical Design of Experiments (DOE) techniques for efficient data collection, analysis and interpretation. Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), including blocking and nesting, in full and fractional factorial designs. Robust design, including classical response surface and Taguchi techniques. Applications to product and process improvement.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENMF
title: Manufacturing Optimization
description: Application of operations research techniques in manufacturing engineering: linear manufacturing optimization problems; transportation, assignment and transshipment problems; dynamic manufacturing programming problems; network problems; manufacturing decision problems.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENMF
title: Special Problems in Manufacturing Engineering
description: Designed to provide graduate students, especially at the PhD level, with the opportunity of pursuing advanced studies in particular areas under the direction of a faculty member. Students would be required to consider problems of an advanced nature.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ENMF
title: CAD/CAM/CAE
description: Components of CAD/CAM/CAE systems. Geometric modeling. Development of customized CAD systems. Complex shape modeling. Computer-aided process planning. CNC machining. Additive Manufacturing. Analysis in computer-aided engineering. Engineering optimization. Virtual design and manufacturing.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENMF
title: Manufacturing of Polymer Composites
description:
Overview of the considerations and challenges in processing fibre-reinforced polymer composites.  Introduction and discussion of constituent materials, reactive polymer composites, thermoplastic composites, textile preforms, autoclave processing, pultrusion, thermoforming, filament winding, liquid composite molding, process modelling, testing and characterization techniques.

Also known as: (formerly Manufacturing Engineering 619.03)
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - B, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ENMG
title: Electricity Regulation
description: An examination of energy development and the business, law and policy issues arising from the development of different electricity sources (nuclear and renewable energy sources).

Permeability, porosity, saturation, capillarity, wettability, relative permeability, interactions between rocks and fluids. Reservoir fluids classification, fluid models, properties, and phase behaviour for subsurface energy applications. Examples from diverse applications including geothermal energy, hydrocarbon recovery, and carbon sequestration.

subject: ENPE

Leakage monitoring using well logs, geothermal fluid leakage monitoring, applications of well log to subsurface energy pathways.

Innovations and technological advancements in geothermal drilling. Special topics including directional drilling; blowout control; logging and coring; hole stability; planning and cost control; underbalanced drilling; drilling geopressured reservoirs; coiled tubing drilling; offshore operations; health, safety, and environmental aspects.

Reserve estimation and management using volumetric and material balance methods in gas, gas-condensate and oil reservoirs. Reservoir drive mechanisms; frontal advanced theory; diagnosis and flow characteristics of gas; water influx in aquifer models; decline curve analysis. Principles of recovery mechanisms for low mobility reservoirs such as oil sands and shales.

Development and coding of 1D and 2D simulation models for single-phase and multi-phase fluid flow. Applications in subsurface energy and environmental engineering, including geothermal energy harvesting, groundwater hydrology, oil and gas engineering, CO2 sequestration, and hydrogen storage.
