description: This case study-based course explores the impacts that resource (minerals, metals, water, fossil fuels) exploration and development has had on the lives of Indigenous people worldwide. The course will discuss historical and present-day examples, with a focus on what happened in different parts of the world and what can be learned moving forward in a better way.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0), No Prerequisite

subject: ERTH
title: Science of Climate Change
description:
Science of Earth's climate system. Content includes how the Earth is influenced by the Sun, cycles and planetary motion, the composition of our atmosphere, the carbon cycle, and global circulation patterns in our oceans and atmosphere, including an exploration of Earth's climate history. Also explores current climate related phenomena (e.g. wildfires, atmospheric rivers, permafrost degradation) and impacts of climate change on both the environment and society, today and in the near future.

Also known as: (formerly Geology 297.01 (Science of Climate Change))
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ERTH
title: Gemology: The Science of Glitter
description:
Gemstones have played an important role in society for hundreds of years. The crystal chemical properties of gems are explained, including the formation, collection, and treatment for producing jewelry with improved characteristics of colour, style, appearance, and durability. Marketing of gems and ethical mining are explored. The use of advanced non-destructive techniques for obtaining gem properties are also discussed.

Also known as: (formerly Geology 297.02 (Gemology: Science of Glitter), Earth 299. 01 (Science of Glitter) )
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Dinosaurs
description:
Biology, evolution, and extinction of dinosaurs; geographic and temporal distribution, habitats, and ecology of the various dinosaur groups; preservation, exploration, collection, preparation, and identification of dinosaur fossils. 

Also known as: (formerly Geology 305)
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-1T)

subject: ERTH
title: Science of Jurassic Park
description: Investigation of how the science of palaeontology is portrayed in film and popular culture. Focus on dinosaurs, their diversity, their evolutionary trends, how we obtain information from the rock record, and how that information is disseminated to the public.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ERTH
title: Geological History of Life
description:
The history of life from the earliest records to the present. Fossils, geological time, extinction, basic paleontology. The rise and development of various animals and plants including dinosaurs, mammals and humans. 

Also known as: (formerly Geology 307)
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ERTH
title: Geology and Human Health
description: An overview of human health issues related to geological phenomena. Examples of possible topics include medical geology, heavy metals in groundwater, effects of volcanic eruptions, effects of asbestos-type minerals, acid mine drainage and soil nutrient deficiencies.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ERTH
title: Field Studies of Earth
description: Field-based study of Earth oriented toward non-majors. Study and interpretation of geological and/or geophysical information in the field, and its significance to social and environmental issues. Field studies will normally be conducted away from Calgary in the spring or summer semester (destinations vary).
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (80-100 Hours), Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related, Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ERTH
title: Minerals and Rocks
description: Systematic description and classification of minerals, rocks, and ores. Characterization of minerals using macroscopic and microscopic properties, especially structure and chemical composition. Use of textures and mineralogy to understand first-order conditions of formation of common sedimentary, igneous, metamorphic, and ore-related rocks.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Fundamentals of Geochemistry
description: Chemical composition of Earth and Earth materials (minerals, rocks, water) with focus on the controls of abundance relationships of the elements and the processes governing the differentiation, migration and distribution of the elements. Fundamentals of radiogenic and stable isotope fractionation and applications. Equilibrium thermodynamics and its applications to construct and interpret phase diagrams; Introduction to geochemical analytical techniques; various applications of geochemical tools.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Earth Surface Processes and Environments
description: Earth surface and near-surface processes and the variety of environments they create and modify at a range of spatial and temporal scales. Investigation of systems and conditions that control the weathering, transport, and deposition of Earth materials, with emphasis on applications to the sedimentary rock cycle and soil formation.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Water and Earth
description: Processes controlling water movement and storage above, on, and beneath Earth's surface. Collection, analysis, and interpretation of hydrological, geophysical, and water quality data at a variety of spatial and temporal scales. Examination of impacts of natural and human activities on water resources, including issues related to water quality, availability, and sustainability.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Rock Deformation and Structures
description: Processes and mechanisms of rock deformation at plate tectonic to microscopic scales and a range of temporal scales (seconds to millions of years). Description of deformation features and analysis of the forces that cause them.
prerequisites_raw: 3 units from Earth 210, Geology 201, 202; and 3 units from Mathematics 211 or 213, Geology 343; and Physics 211 or 221.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ERTH
title: Climate, Evolution, and Deep Time
description: Earth's climate system and life, and the geologic record of how they have changed through time. Investigation of the geologic data used to reconstruct past intervals of climate and biological upheaval with comparison to modern rates of change.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Global Geophysics and Planetary Geoscience
description: Application of physical principles to understanding Earth and other bodies in the Solar System. Examination of evidence for Earth formation and structure considering thermodynamics, gravity, seismology, and magnetism. Analysis of Earth's lithosphere including plate motion, earthquakes, and comparison of oceanic and continental crust.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ERTH
title: Computers in the Earth and Environmental Sciences
description: Topics in statistical analysis emphasizing geoscientific applications. Error analysis, Taylor series, curve fitting, statistical analysis of spatial data, multivariate data analysis, interpolation. Numerical algorithms for estimation of model parameters. Objective functions, norms, curve fitting, linear least squares regression, and linearization of models/data. Use of spreadsheet software and Python for implementation.
prerequisites_raw: 3 units from Earth 330, Earth 360, Geology 401, Geophysics 351; Mathematics 211; Mathematics 267 or 277; 3 units from Computer Science 217, 231, 235, Data Science 211
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Science of Natural Disasters in Popular Culture
description: Investigation of how geoscience is portrayed in the media with special attention given to natural disasters. Discussion of causes and drivers of natural disasters and how they can be predicted, prevented, or mitigated, and how the media can help and/or hinder our understanding of and reaction to these events.
antirequisites_raw: Credit for Earth 374 and either Earth 375 or Geophysics 375 will not be allowed.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ERTH
title: Natural Disasters and Critical Earth Phenomena
description: Causes of disasters such as earthquakes, tsunami, volcanic eruptions, mud flows, landslides, avalanches, flooding, tornadoes and hurricanes, and other critical phenomena such as sinkholes, ozone depletion and radiation, carbon dioxide and global warming, El Niño, toxic natural materials and pollution, and extraterrestrial impacts. Surveys of historic disasters and their effects on life on Earth. Methods of prediction and prevention of disasters and precautions for the mitigation of their effects.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ERTH
title: Geoscience Field School
description: The development of field-based techniques in the collection, description, analysis, interpretation, and reporting of geoscientific field data and results. Includes navigation, geological mapping, field sampling, and geophysical methods. Multiple days of field work outside of the classroom in methods related to each of geology, hydrogeology, and geophysics.
prerequisites_raw: Earth 210 and 290.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (80-120 Hours), Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related, Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: ERTH
title: Topics in Earth
description: Exploration of various areas in Earth. Topics will vary from year-to-year. It will be offered as required to provide the opportunity for students to engage in additional areas in Earth. Before registration, consult the Department of Earth for topics offered.
prerequisites_raw: Consent of the Department.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0) or (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Igneous Petrology
description: Petrogenesis and tectonic setting of igneous rocks using field data, geochemistry and experiments. Identification and interpretation of igneous rocks based on mineralogy and texture. Application of igneous petrology to Earth processes and evolution.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Metamorphic Petrology
description: Petrogenesis and tectonic setting of metamorphic rocks using field data, geochemistry and experiments. Identification and interpretation of metamorphic rocks based on mineralogy and texture. Application of metamorphic petrology to Earth processes and evolution.
course_attributes: GFC Hours (3-3), Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A

subject: ERTH
title: Sedimentary Petrology
description: Origin, occurrence, structure and diagenetic history of siliciclastic and carbonate sedimentary rocks. Consideration of provenance of transported components, and origin of biotic and abiotic constituents. Diagenetic history of rocks and its effects on mineralogy, texture, structures, porosity, and permeability. Laboratory includes hand specimens and thin-section petrography.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Sedimentary Facies Models
description: Multiscale description and interpretation of a range of terrestrial and marine sedimentary depositional settings of clastic, chemical/biochemical, and carbonaceous sedimentary rocks. Distinction of sedimentary facies and facies successions based on recognition of characteristic lithologies, structures, fossil content or geochemical composition, as applicable. Discussion of the mechanisms by which the biological, climatic, and geological evolution of the Earth is recorded in sedimentary rocks.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Physical Hydrology and Hydrogeology
description: Hydrologic cycle, conservation principle, Darcy's Law, river and lake systems, groundwater flow systems, groundwater – surface water interaction, aquifer testing, soil hydrology, effective stress and geotechnical considerations, solute transport in groundwater.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Aqueous Geochemical Processes
description: Theoretical and applied aspects of aqueous geochemistry. Methods for collection and preservation of water samples in the field; laboratory analysis of water samples; theory and application of aqueous thermochemical models; biogeochemistry; applications and case studies. Includes a one-day, weekend field trip during the first several weeks of class.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Tectonics and Structural Geology
description: Foundations of structural analysis, brittle and plastic deformation mechanism, quantitative assessment of rock deformation at various scales. Simple statistical analysis of data; applications to tectonic settings and the exploration of natural resources, cross-sections and advanced map interpretation; tectonics; neotectonics.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Paleoclimate, Extinction, and Recovery through Geologic Time
description: Investigating major upheavals in global systems throughout geologic time using paleoclimatic and paleontological data. How varying magnitudes and rates of change have affected climatic and biological systems. Morphology and taxonomy of fossil groups and geological applications.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (4-0)

subject: ERTH
title: Applied Geophysics and Interpretation
description: Geophysical surveying methods applied to resource exploration, environmental monitoring, and engineering applications. Surveying theory and interpretation for refraction seismic, reflection seismic, gravity, electrical and electromagnetic methods. Analysis and integration of geophysical and geological data. Qualitative and quantitative interpretation. Industrial case studies.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Geoscientific Signal Processing
description: Analysis of geophysical time series using one dimensional and multidimensional digital signal processing theory. Practical applications using commercial and open-source computational software.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Continuum Geomechanics and Numerical Modelling
description: Topics in partial differential equations and numerical analysis emphasizing geophysics applications. Forward modelling of linear elliptic and hyperbolic PDEs: Poisson equation, Laplace equation, and acoustic wave equation. Taylor series, numerical differentiation and integration, numerical solution of ODEs and PDEs using finite difference and finite element techniques. Use of computer packages to implement numerical solutions.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Ore Deposits
description: Processes of formation of metallic ore and diamond deposits. Classification of ores based on petrologic association. Introduction to ore microscopy in reflected light.
prerequisites_raw: 3 units from Earth 410 or Geology 431; 3 units from Earth 415 or Geology 433.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Applied Minerology
description: Crystal symmetry, space groups, X-ray diffraction techniques, and introduction to crystal structure determination and refinement using experimental data sets. Emphasis is on the interpretation and application of results to solving problems in Earth Sciences.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Sequence Stratigraphy and Basin Analysis
description: Fundamental concepts of petroleum geology including deposition/maturation and facies analysis of source rocks; basin stratigraphy, subsidence, deformation, and thermal history; hydrocarbon generation, migration, and accumulation. Principles of sequence stratigraphy, hydrocarbon production, subsurface geological analysis applied to the evaluation and quantification of oil and gas reservoirs. Case studies and applications from petroleum basins from around the world.
prerequisites_raw: 3 units from Earth 320 or Geology 381; 3 units from Earth 340 or Geology 445; 3 units from Earth 420, Geology 463, Geology 483, Geophysics 457.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Groundwater and Surface Water Quality
description: Chemical and biological processes in surface water and groundwater systems. Water quality standards and regulation, contaminant transport and dispersal, fluid-sediment interactions, remediation of contamination, field approaches for delineation of contamination. Review of the partial differential equations and boundary conditions that describe groundwater flow and transport. Techniques will include the use of thermochemical models, numerical modelling of contaminant migration, and examination of case studies.
prerequisites_raw: 3 units from Earth 430 or Geology 401; 3 units from Earth 435 or Geology 403.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Geohazards and Geotechnical Analysis
description: The role of geology in engineering problems. Characterization of soil, rock, and rock masses. Mechanical behaviour of geologic material. Landslides and slope stability analysis. Investigation methods and case histories.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Evolution of Earth
description: Integration of petrology, major, trace element and stable and radiogenic isotope geochemistry to evolution of lithosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere. Stages of Earth's history including planetary accretion, core formation, evolution of mantle, differentiation of bulk silicate earth, evolution of continental crust and its tectonic mechanisms, evolution of continental mantle lithosphere, evolution of atmosphere and hydrosphere.
prerequisites_raw: 3 units from Earth 315 or Geology 323; 3 units from Earth 340 or Geology 445; 3 units from Earth 360 or Geophysics 351; 3 units from Earth 410, Earth 415, Geology 431, Geology 433; 3 units from Earth 450, Geology 475, Geology 493.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Global and Applied Seismology
description: Theory of acoustic and elastic wave propagation applied to global and exploration seismology. Topics include constitutive models, boundary conditions, investigations into the seismic source, and structural studies. Applications to resource exploration, broadband observations, and environmental monitoring.
prerequisites_raw: 3 units from Earth 460 or Geophysics 355; 3 units from Earth 467 or Geophysics 517; 3 units from Earth 365, Earth 468, Geophysics 419, Geophysics 420; Physics 321.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Mining and Environmental Geophysics
description: Theory of gravity, magnetic, resistivity, induced polarization, self-potential, and radiometric methods. Gravitational and magnetic fields of Earth. Large-scale, low-resolution applications to global geophysics and mineral exploration. Small-scale, high-resolution applications to geological, geotechnical, hydrological, and environmental monitoring.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Signal Processing and Inversion Techniques
description: Analysis and processing of multidimensional geophysics data using theoretical and practical concepts of digital signal processing and geophysical inversion. Topics may include reverse time migration, least squares, maximum entropy, singular value decomposition, regularization, stochastic approaches, and iterative techniques such as conjugate gradients. Practical applications using commercial and open-source computational software.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Independent Study
description: A written report and a public presentation based on independent study. Originality is emphasized, laboratory and field studies are encouraged.
prerequisites_raw: Science 311; and consent of the Department and of a departmental faculty member.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (0-9), Entrepreneurial Thinking - Focused, Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: ERTH
title: Senior Thesis
description: A written report and a public presentation based on extensive independent study. Originality is emphasized, laboratory and field studies are encouraged.
prerequisites_raw: Science 311; and consent of the Department and of a departmental faculty member who will act as a supervisor.
course_attributes: Entrepreneurial Thinking - Focused, Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (0-9), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: ERTH
title: Advanced Field Methods
description: Field-based study of complex geoscience topics. Advanced skills development in one or more aspects of field data collection, portrayal, description, analysis, and interpretation. Field work will normally be conducted away from Calgary in the spring or summer semester (destinations vary).
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (80-120 Hours), Entrepreneurial Thinking - Focused, Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: ERTH
title: Topics in Earth
description: Courses are offered in contemporary topics in areas such as electrical and electromagnetic methods, exploration and environmental geophysics, geochemistry, gravity and magnetics, hydrogeology, integrated geophysical methods, mineralogy, paleontology, petroleum geology, petrology, quantitative geology, sedimentology, seismology, structural geology, and surficial geology.
prerequisites_raw: 78 units and consent of the Department.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0) or (3-3)

subject: ERTH
title: Advanced Igneous Petrology
description: Emphasis on critical analysis, independent investigation, and communication of results at the graduate level.
prerequisites_raw: Admission to a graduate-level Geoscience program.

title: Geochemical Laboratory Methods
description: An overview of geochemical analytical methods (XRD, Raman Spectroscopy, SEM, FESEM, EPMA, XRF, ICP-MS, MS, organic geochemical analyses, etc.) in geoscience and their applications. Provides the theoretical background of the techniques as well as opportunities for practical experience. Particular emphasis will be placed on analytical techniques available within the department.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-2)

description: Review of the partial differential equations and boundary conditions that describe groundwater flow and transport. Introduction to numerical methods. The course emphasizes the practical aspects of building groundwater and transport models using computer exercises and a groundwater modeling project. Emphasis on critical analysis, independent investigation, and communication of results at an advanced level.

subject: ERTH
title: Unconventional Reservoir Characterization and Evaluation for Transitional Energy
description: Fundamentals of fluid storage and production in unconventional (coal/shale/tight) reservoirs, core analysis methods, field-based reservoir and fracture characterization methods using rate- and pressure-transient analysis and diagnostic fracture injection test analyses; applications to hydrocarbon reservoirs and subsurface transitional energy pathways including geothermal energy, carbon storage, hydrogen production and storage and critical elements.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0)

title: Advanced Global and Applied Seismology
description: Emphasis on critical analysis, independent investigation, and communication of results at the graduate level.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-3)

title: (PHYS 663) Applications of Stable Isotopes
description: Application of stable isotope techniques across the geosciences and related fields to study water, carbon, nitrogen, and sulphur cycles and their interactions, with applications in hydrology, paleoclimate, geothermometry, fossil fuel exploration, pollutant tracing, food webs, and forensic investigations.

course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (0-6)

subject: ERTH
title: Advanced Geoscience Field Studies
description: Application of advanced concepts and/or methods to field problems of current interest.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (80-100 Hours)

subject: ERTH
title: Advanced Special Topics in Earth
description: Courses are offered in specific topics in areas such as geochemistry, hydrogeology, mineralogy, paleontology, petroleum geology, petrology, quantitative geology, sedimentology, structural geology, surficial geology, seismology, environmental geophysics, potential methods, integrated geophysical studies, and geodynamics.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0) or (3-3)

subject: ESCI
title: Energy Use in the Modern World
description: Overview of how the world's energy systems work and why these energy systems are essential to how society functions. Examination of benefits and drawbacks of the sources of energy people use; generation and distribution of electricity; energy efficiency; and environmental consequences of energy choices
course_attributes: Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related, Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ESCI
title: Energy Transformations and Heat Engines
description: Introduction to the thermodynamics of how heat engines transform heat into useful forms of energy for electricity and transportation. Examination of using pV diagrams to calculate work; efficiency; waste heat; and changes in entropy.
prerequisites_raw: Energy Science 201, and Chemistry 201 or 202,  and Chemistry 203 or 204, and Mathematics 267 or 277, or admission to Natural Science (Energy Science Concentration); and 3 units from Physics 211, 221, 227; and 3 units from Physics 223, 259, 355.
antirequisites_raw: Credit for Energy Science 317 and Science 507.17 (Engines and Electricity) will not be allowed.  Also known as: (formerly Science 317)
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2T)

subject: ESCI
title: Climate Change Causes, Adaptations, and Mitigations
description: Principles of climate change and the interplay between anthropogenic climate change and energy systems.  Earth's current changing climate; the effects of greenhouse gases and human activity; the impact of climate change on society and the environment; and climate change mitigation and adaptation.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ESCI
title: Topics in Energy Science
description: Discussion of a particular topic on energy science. The topic will be determined by the course instructor and will be communicated to students before the start of term.
prerequisites_raw: Energy Science 201 and admission to Energy Science Major or Minor; and consent of the Department.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-1T or 3-0)

subject: ESCI
title: Nuclear Energy
description: Overview of nuclear energy production, including the nuclear fuel cycle, the workings of atomic nuclei, nuclear reactions, nuclear cross-section, reactor design, uranium mining, waste disposal, and both beneficial and harmful biological effects of radiation.
prerequisites_raw: 3 units from Energy Science 317, Physics 449, or Chemistry 371; or Engineering Energy and Environment 355 and admission to the Schulich School of Engineering.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2T)

subject: ESCI
title: Batteries and Fuel Cells
description: Scientific principles behind batteries and fuel cells, including the electrochemistry of classic voltaic and electrolytic cells; thermodynamics, kinetics, and performance curves of batteries and fuel cells; and current applications and limitations.
prerequisites_raw: 3 units from Energy Science 317, Physics 449, or Chemistry 371; or Engineering Energy and Environment 355 and admission to the Schulich School of Engineering.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2)

subject: ESCI
title: Solar Energy
description: The science behind capturing and using solar energy for human utilization, covering sunlight energy conversion; solar photovoltaic systems; integration of solar power into energy systems; and environmental, societal, and economic issues related to solar project development.
prerequisites_raw: 3 units from Energy Science 317, Physics 449, or Chemistry 371; or Engineering Energy and Environment 355 and admission to the Schulich School of Engineering.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2T)

subject: ESCI
title: Energy from Water
description: Introduction to the fundamentals of utilizing energy from water in the environment.   Examination of hydrology and fluid dynamics; electricity generation from rivers, ocean waves, tides, and ocean currents; pumped storage; and environmental, societal, and economic issues.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2)

subject: ESCI
title: Geothermal Energy
description: Overview of utilizing thermal energy from the ground, including low and high temperature geothermal systems; ground-source heat pumps; geothermal heating; and related technical, environmental, and socioeconomic issues.
antirequisites_raw: Credit for Energy Science 433 and Science 533 will not be allowed.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2)

subject: ESCI
title: Energy from Biomass
description: Overview of the energy from biomass, including  the production of biomass feedstocks; the conversion of biomass to energy or to feedstocks for other products; the use of biomass in transportation, electricity, and heat generation; its societal impacts such as air pollution; and economic and technical limitations.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2)

subject: ESCI
title: Coal, Oil, and Natural Gas
description: Overview of fossil fuel energy and hydrocarbon systems.  Examining the history and geography of development of fossil fuel resources; upstream, midstream, and downstream components; conventional oil and gas, heavy oil and shale gas/oil resources; liquified natural gas (LNG); abatement of greenhouse gas emissions using carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS); and Indigenous perspectives on Canadian fossil fuel development and extraction.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2)

subject: ESCI
title: Wind Energy
description: Overview of wind energy including generating electricity from wind, including turbine types and relevant fluid dynamics; limitations to wind power such as the Betz limit and variable supply; environmental consequences related to wind energy; interactions between wind power producers, the electricity system, and the environment.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2)

subject: ESCI
title: Mineral Resources for Energy Systems
description: Overview of minerals that are critical to energy science, including economic importance and supply risk; decarbonizing energy systems and the digital economy; the exploration, production, processing, and distribution of critical minerals; and socioeconomic, Indigenous, and environmental perspectives.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2)

subject: ESCI
title: Topics in Energy Science
description: Discussion of a particular topic on energy science at the intermediate level. The topic will be determined by the course instructor and will be communicated to students before the start of term.
prerequisites_raw: 6 units of courses labelled Energy Science (ESCI) and admission to Energy Science Major or Minor; and consent of the Department.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-1T or 3-0)

subject: ESCI
title: Energy Policy
description: Overview of the role of energy policy in energy systems including the history of energy policy, the policy making progress, principles of policy analysis and policy communication, and the impact of energy policy on energy systems. The course will cover different aspects of energy policy at the international, national, and subnational level including climate/emissions policy, environmental assessment and review current issues in energy policy.
course_attributes: Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related, Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: ESCI
title: Energy Science Capstone Course
description: Team-based course where students integrate the knowledge and skills from previous courses to critically evaluate local, national, and/or global energy-system scenarios to sustainably deliver the energy society needs into the future.
course_attributes: Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related, Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: ESCI
title: Independent Research in Energy Science
description: An independent study course for students to research a topic related to energy working closely with a faculty member.
prerequisites_raw: 15 units in the Field of Energy Science and consent of the Faculty.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (0-9), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: ESCI
title: Topics in Energy Science

subject: FILM
title: Introduction to Film Studies
description: An introduction to the foundational issues and vocabulary of film studies explored through a wide range of filmic texts. Privileging questions of film technique and style, the course also considers cinema as an institution that comprises an industrial system of production, social and aesthetic norms and codes and particular modes of reception.

subject: FILM
title: Introduction to Research in Film Studies
description: An in-depth introduction to conducting research in film studies, emphasizing critical viewing, reading and writing through the examination of a specific topic, such as a film genre, a national cinema, or a filmmaker.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-3), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: FILM
title: Topics in National Cinema
description:
Topics will explore various aspects of, or historical moments in, a particular nation's cinematic culture. Topics might include Quebecois cinema, current British cinema, German cinema Between the Wars, Canadian cinema, the History of Chinese cinema, etc.

subject: FILM
title: Topic in Cinema and Gender Studies
description:
Topics will explore the representation of gender and sexuality in cinema. Topics might include: Images of Women in the American 1940s, Lesbian Images in Current Cinema, The Queer 1950s, Comparative Images of Women in American and French Cinema, etc.

subject: FILM
title: History Of Popular Cinema
description: An assessment of the various ways in which the history of film production can be approached, including the development of filmmaking technologies, evolutions in cinematic style and narrative traditions, particularly as they relate to popular cinema, and changing industrial practices.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-3)

subject: FILM
title: Issues in Film History
description: An introduction to key concepts in cinematic historiography. Emphasis will be placed upon non-traditional or non-canonical films and their relationship to dominant histories of filmmaking.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-3)

subject: FILM
title: Film Theory up to 1950
description: An introduction to theoretical perspectives on film before the mid twentieth century. Connects film with broader debates on aesthetics, medium specificity, genre, and realism. Includes theories developed in the first half of the 20th century related to Silent Film, Formalism, Montage, Critical Theory, and Auteur theories.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-3)

subject: FILM
title: Film Theory After 1950
description: An introduction to theoretical perspectives on film developed since the mid-twentieth century, specifically Structuralism, Linguistics, Psycholanalysis, Feminism, Post-structuralism, Cultural Studies, Post-colonialism and Queer Theory.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-3)

subject: FILM
title: Canadian Film
description: An introduction to key historical and theoretical aspects of Canadian film. Topics will include the study of Canadian film auteurs, documentary and social change, feature film genres, and the role of government regulations. Explores the central themes and issues facing Canadian filmmakers and audiences.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-3)

subject: FILM
title: Topic in Film Theory
description: Topics will be organized around particular theorists, schools of theory, historical issues in film culture, or contemporary thought on film. Topics may include: Psychoanalysis and/as Film Theory; Kaja Silverman and Teresa de Lauretis; Modernism and Postmodernism; Feminist Film Theory; Queer Theory and Film; Postcolonial Theory and Film; Semiotics.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-3)

subject: FILM
title: Topic in the Director's Cinema
description: Topics will examine the distinctive style and concerns of a particular director or directors.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-3)

subject: FILM
title: Advanced Topics in Film Genre
description: Topics will be organized around a specific film generic tradition.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-3)

subject: FILM
title: Experiential Learning in Film
description: This course is designed to provide students with the opportunity to combine interests in film studies research with experiential learning opportunities in the community and workplace (internships, paid employment, approved film production training or volunteer position).
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (6-12 HOURS), WIL Internship

subject: FILM
title: Special Topics in Film Studies
description: Topic may be historical, theoretical or analytical in emphasis.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-3), WIL Field Placement

subject: FILM
title: The Film Festival
description: An exploration of the social practices (cultural tourism, tastemaking, identity formation, celebrity and star formation) and operational aspects (marketing, promotion, jurying, lobbying, audience cultivation) of film festivals. Students will be encouraged to participate in community service learning through volunteer opportunities with a particular festival.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-3), Entrepreneurial Thinking - Focused

subject: FILM
title: The Canadian Film Industry: National and Global Perspectives
description: A study of the nature of the Canadian film industry. Emphasis will be on the evolution of the Canadian motion picture industry in the twentieth century and how it is situated in contemporary popular culture. Other topics include Canada's historic relationship to Hollywood, the audience for Canadian films, the role of the state in funding, distribution and production systems, the impact of new technologies, and how the structure of Canada's film industry compares with those of other countries.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-3)

subject: FILM
title: Film Audience and Reception
description: Explores aspects of spectatorship, audience and reception approaches as they intersect with the experience and study of cinema.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-3)

subject: FILM
title: Experimental Film and Video
description: Explores the genre of experimental film and video. Particular emphasis will be given to the history and evolution of works in this genre with attention to Canadian contributions and the impact of digital and new media.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-3)

subject: FILM
title: Independent Research in Film Studies
description: Supervised individual study of a special topic.

subject: FILM
title: Advanced Special Topics in Film Studies
description: Selected topic in film studies suitable for advanced studies in the degree. Topic may be historical, theoretical or analytical in emphasis.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-3)

subject: FILM
title: Capstone Seminar in Film Studies
description: Explores the variety of ways in which film and the technologies of motion pictures connect with social life with reference to a specific topic. Completion of a major project that will integrate understanding of film theory, history and genres.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-3), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: FILM
title: Honours Seminar
description: Individual research and seminar activities (e.g., critiques, presentations, and peer reviews of drafts) to produce a proposal and a paper to be used as the basis for the honours thesis.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2S-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: FILM
title: Honours Thesis
description: Supervised individual research and preparation of an honours thesis. Incorporating material from the Film 595 final paper, to complete the honours thesis. Seminar activities include progress reports, peer reviews, and support for poster presentations and oral exams.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (1S-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: FNCE
title: Financial Management
description: An introduction to the allocation of financial capital, from a theoretical as well as a practical perspective. The course builds on a modern understanding of how risk, time horizon, and market imperfections each affect the value of real and financial assets. Topics include time value of money, the risk-return trade off, financial investing, corporate financing, and corporate investing.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - E, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-3T) or (3-1.5T)

subject: FNCE
title: Canadian Business Finance
description: An introduction to business financial management practices in Canada including investment decision, capital markets, and sources, uses and costs of capital over short, intermediate and long run situations.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - E, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: FNCE
title: Personal Financial Management
description: An introduction to personal financial management practices in Canada. Topics discussed may include goal setting, personal financial statements, the mathematics of personal finance, taxation, general and life insurance, retirement planning, investments, and estate planning. Completion of the course should enable students to properly prepare and plan their own financial future.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - E, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-3T), Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related

subject: FNCE
title: Security Analysis and Investments
description: A comprehensive exploration of security analysis and investments aimed at advancing understanding of financial markets, valuation techniques, and portfolio selection under various investment objectives. Topics such as capital allocation, diversification, security (stocks, bonds, derivatives) valuation, and market efficiency are covered.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - E, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: FNCE
title: Futures and Options
description: A study of financial contracts for which the payoffs are contingent upon or derived from the value pre-specified underlying economic variables. Typical underlying variables include the spot price of a commodity and the price of a stock. These contracts are used extensively for hedging and speculative purposes. They also provide useful information about forecasts of the underlying economic variable in a process called "price discovery".
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - E, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: FNCE
title: Capital Budgeting
description: Capital investment policies, real options, required rate of return calculation, tax factors, risk analysis, buy versus lease, abandonment considerations.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - E, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: FNCE
title: Trading and Market Data Management
description: Introduction to accessing data feeds as they are used by professional financial market traders and analysts. Data for stock, bond, futures and options markets, accounting statements and securities commission filings, as well as real-time and historical news events and analysis will be studied.
prerequisites_raw: Admission to the Haskayne School of Business and Finance 317.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - E, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: FNCE
title: Corporate Finance

course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - E, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: FNCE
title: International Finance
description: A study of the forces affecting the financial environment of the corporate sector which appear to stem from requirements in the international sector. Balance-of-payments problems, exchange rates, currency risk hedging techniques, international reserve creations and transfers are some of the major elements studied.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - E, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: FNCE
title: Portfolio Theory and Management
description: Analysis of the major aspects of the grouping of financial assets. Portfolio analysis and its application to portfolio management, capital market theory and the measurement of financial performance in the presence of risk.

subject: FNCE

course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - E, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: FNCE
title: Financial Risk Management
description: A framework for evaluating financial risks and managing them with the use of financial securities including derivatives. Includes firm valuation with risk management, value-at-risk, testing financial models, optimal hedging strategies, energy risk management, market risk, static versus dynamic strategies, interest rate risk, credit risk and liquidity risk. Case analysis of financial disasters due to risk management failures.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - E, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-1T)

subject: FNCE
title: UCeed Haskayne Student Fund
description: A comprehensive hands-on course on the financing of early-stage companies. subject: GEOG
title: Global Environmental Change
description: Examination of current environmental issues related to physical geography, including topics such as climate change, energy and sustainable resource development, weather extremes, and natural hazards. The course uses contemporary topics to introduce fundamental principles of physical and environmental geography while highlighting societal impacts and influences.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0) or (3-1/2T)

subject: GEOG
title: Society and Environment
description: Foundations of human geography presented with integrative case studies of current and urgent human-environment issues from global to regional to local. Examines the complex interconnections between humans and environment using topics such as climate change, sustainability, development, poverty, food, urbanization, and technologies of the digital age.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0) or (3-1/2T)

subject: GEOG
title: Thinking Spatially in a Digital World
description: Introduces mapping technologies and digital spatial data for solving geographical problems that focus on how to collect, manage, analyze, and communicate diverse spatial data. Topics include geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing, spatial statistics, geovisualization, cartography, and web mapping.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0) or (3-1/2T), No Prerequisite, Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: GEOG
title: Introduction to Climate Change
description: Introduction to climate change science, climate change impacts, and Canadian and international climate policy. Topics include an introduction to the atmosphere, ocean, and cryosphere, the carbon cycle, the greenhouse effect, natural climate variability in Earth history, climate models, and an overview of economic, political, social, and policy dimensions of climate change.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0), No Prerequisite

subject: GEOG
title: Climate and Ecosystems
description: Introduction to the Earth's atmospheric environment (elements and controls of climate and their implications for hydrology, vegetation, and soils) and the nature and distribution of ecosystems and vegetation. Incorporates interactions between humans and their environment, especially those leading to global change on the decade to century time-scale.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2)

subject: GEOG
title: Landforms and Soils
description: Introduction to physical landscapes and soils, emphasizing the formation and geographic distribution of mountains, volcanoes, valleys, and deserts, and their shaping by rivers and glaciers; and the fundamental concepts in soil science. Incorporates human modification of the Earth's surface.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: GEOG
title: Society and Environmental Change
description: Environmental and resource issues, with emphasis on topics such as climate change, sustainability, ethics, planning, policy and decision making, and management strategies. Case examples highlight issues in resource sectors such as freshwater, oceans, parks and wildlife, tourism and recreation, forests and energy.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0) or (3-1/2T), Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related, Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: GEOG
title: Geographies of Canada
description: Exploration of what it means to be Canadian in a global context. Examination of the historic, cultural, social, political, economic, and environmental factors that promote unity and inter-regional tensions.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0), Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related

subject: GEOG
title: Geographies of East and Southeast Asia
description: An introduction to the geographies of East and Southeast Asia utilizing the foundations of physical and human geography. The logical divisions based on culture, physiography, history, migration, social and economic both currently and historically. Issues of development and the environmental impacts relating to rapid growth, urbanization, and intensive use of resources will be addressed.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0), WIL Field Placement, Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related, Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: GEOG
title: Geographies of Europe
description: An introduction to the geographies of Europe utilizing the foundations of physical and human geography. The logical divisions based on culture, physiography, history, migration, social, and economy will be explored both currently and historically. Settlement patterns, transportation networks, urban and environmental sustainability, economic activities, and contrasting cultural, ethnic, linguistic and religious variations will be emphasized.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0), WIL Field Placement, Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related, Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: GEOG
title: Political, Economic, and Urban Geography
description: A introduction to the major concepts of human geography including political geography, economic geography, the uneven distribution of development across the surface of the Earth, and the urbanization of the developed and developing world.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2), Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related

subject: GEOG
title: Social and Cultural Geography
description: An introduction to the major concepts of human geography including demography, migration, cultures, languages, and religions.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2)

subject: GEOG
title: Geospatial Communication
description: An introduction to fundamentals in cartography, remote sensing, geographic information systems, and descriptive spatial statistics.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2)

subject: GEOG
title: International Field Studies
description: An introduction to conducting international reconnaissance research in geography. Provides a background in various aspects of ethical research practices, qualitative and quantitative data collection, analysis, and dissemination.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (1-2), WIL Field Placement, Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: GEOG
title: Geographic Field Studies
description: An introduction to field research techniques and topics in physical and human geography. Lectures and projects will provide an introduction to a range of geographic disciplines. Field exercises will normally be conducted away from Calgary for about ten days before Fall Term.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (70 HOURS), WIL Field Placement, Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: GEOG
title: Meteorology and Hydrology
description: Atmospheric connections with the hydrological cycle, including evapotranspiration, water vapour, stability, cloud development, and precipitation. Water transport is followed through soil moisture, groundwater, and stream flow. Discussed methods focus on tracking water transport through the land-atmosphere system at various scales. Additional topics may include water quality, water resource management, and hydrology of selected landscapes.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: GEOG
title: Process Geomorphology
description: A systematic study of the physical processes that shape the Earth's surface. Emphasis is on the mechanics of geomorphic processes and their interaction with Earth materials.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-1), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: GEOG
title: Soil Science
description: Exploration of soil science including the chemical, physical, and biological properties of soils; soil formation and development, including the classification of soils, and the application of soil science to land use, environmental quality, global change, and sustainable development.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-1), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: GEOG
title: Climate Change and Society
description: Overview of social dimensions of climate change. Addresses representation, governance, knowledge production, power and justice. Examines how responses and policies are shaped across various scales including global, national, regional, urban and individual.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: GEOG
title: Sustainability and Political Ecology
description: Exploration of the challenges associated with environmental management and governance, particularly in terms of achieving sustainability. Emphasis is placed on ongoing local, regional, and global environmental problems, using political ecology perspectives to understand power, discourse and interest mechanisms behind environmental rights, controls, and sustainability needs.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-1T), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: GEOG
title: Animal Geography
description: Explores the socio-spatial relationships between humans and animals, with the goal of elucidating the ecological, economic, political, social, and cultural pressures shaping these relations, and the conflicts arising from human-animal interactions. Inter-species bonds and emotional lives of animals are also covered.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-1T), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: GEOG
title: Global Change and Hazards
description: Examination of the factors that influence vulnerability and resiliency to environmental hazards. Emphasis on how human activities change both the dynamics of natural processes and the spatio-temporal variability of vulnerability and resiliency.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-1/2T), WIL Field Placement, Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: GEOG
title: Field Studies in Social and Economic Geography
description: Field research and reconnaissance survey techniques. Individual and group travel-study combined with formal instruction and seminars.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (36-48 HOURS), WIL Field Placement, Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: GEOG
title: Field Studies in Physical and Environmental Geography
description: Field research and reconnaissance survey techniques. Individual and group travel-study combined with formal instruction and seminars.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (36-48 HOURS), WIL Field Placement, Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: GEOG
title: Urban Social Geography
description: Concepts of urban geography with particular reference to intra-urban social issues.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-1)

subject: GEOG
title: Economic Geography
description: Theories, concepts and techniques of economic geography with emphasis on policy issues relating to examples at the urban, regional, and national levels.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-1T), Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related, Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: GEOG
title: Uneven Development
description: Foundations of development geography and its concern with multiscalar, multidimensional processes of intervention and change. Focus on urban-rural and global-local change effects and human settlement. An interrogation of globalization, poverty, marginality, human settlement and the diversity of development actors, the state, the aid community, and the people directly affected by development.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-1T), Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related

subject: GEOG
title: Political Geographies
description: Spatial study of political systems, structures, and processes, and their relationship to geographic factors.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0), Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related

subject: GEOG
title: Cartography and Geovisualization
description: Focuses on mapping technologies for cartography and geo-visualization. The role of cartography and geovisualization is explored both theoretically, and practically in the communication of spatial data. In lecture and lab-based settings, examines data considerations, map design fundamentals and techniques, map use and interactive design for the communication of geographic information.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2)

subject: GEOG
title: Geographic Information Systems and Science
description: The technical and theoretical foundations of Geographic Information Science. Explorations of data types and structures, data integrity, metadata, data acquisition and maintenance, analytical techniques, and methods for geovisualization will be explored in lecture and laboratory.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: GEOG
title: Ways of Knowing in Geography
description: Conceptualizing human-environment realities into research: an introduction to philosophical foundations of ways of thinking and critical perspectives; qualitative and mixed methods approaches. Examination of 'rules' of research and the challenges of real world complexities. In-depth examples of human-environment research from theory to practice, broad research design and proposal writing practice.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-1T), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: GEOG
title: Remote Sensing Essentials
description: Instruction in the background, use and interpretation of remote sensing imagery. subject: GEOG
title: Critical Zone Science
description: Examination of the Critical Zone, Earth's outer layer that extends from the top of vegetation to the bottom of the fresh groundwater zone. It is a constantly evolving boundary layer where rock, soil, water, air, and living organisms interact to regulate the landscape and natural habitats, and determine the availability of life-sustaining resources, including our food production and water quality.

subject: GEOG

Draws on physical, chemical, and biological sciences to understand linked topics such as Arctic glaciers, marine environments, hydrology, permafrost, wildlife, vegetation, and sea ice. Particular focus is paid to cycles of carbon, water, and energy as key drivers of the Arctic system. Selected human interactions with the Arctic system are also examined.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: GEOG

subject: GEOG

These physical processes are then linked to controls on primary production in the ocean, and marine foodwebs/ecosystems. Chemical processes driven by circulation and biology are examined, with a focus on marine feedbacks related to past and present climate change.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2)

subject: GEOG

subject: GEOG

Topics focus on bioregions, biodiversity, communities, ecosystems at multiple scales, as well as investigation of ways that human and natural disturbance affect these patterns. Uses qualitative and quantitative approaches to measure these effects to inform management and conservation.

Through theoretical and case study articles, discussions of themes such as water, food, green space, housing, waste, and through local case-studies, students will examine the evolution of urban political ecology, its main tenets and its relevance for understanding urbanization processes.

subject: LAW
title: Constitutional Law
description: The basic elements of Canadian constitutional law. The nature of constitutions and constitutional processes; principles of constitutional interpretation; constitutional amendment; Federal-Provincial distribution of legislative powers including the federal general power, natural resources and public property, provincial property and civil rights, trade and commerce, provincial taxation, transportation, communications, and criminal law; the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms including principles of limitation, remedies, interpretation, application, fundamental freedoms, democratic and language rights, mobility rights, legal rights, equality rights, and aboriginal people's rights.

subject: LAW
title: Contracts
description: A legal and policy analysis of the basic principles and fundamental concepts of the law of contracts as they relate to commercial and consumer transactions. The formation of contracts including offer and acceptance and, consideration; estoppel; privity; terms of contract, including exemption clauses; standard form contracts; bailment; mistake, misrepresentation and unconscionability; termination, including the doctrine of frustration; breach and remedies for breach; dispute resolution processes. Emphasis is placed not only on a knowledge of rules and principles, their historical derivation, rationale, efficacy and social validity, but also upon their creative use to both avoid and resolve disputes.

subject: LAW
title: Legislation
description: The fundamentals of the legislative process: policy development, legislative drafting, public bill processes, statutory interpretation. The interaction of law and policy in the development of legislation and statutory interpretation. Substantive law connections are made with other first year courses. The functions of the lawyer within these processes are examined, including issues of professional responsibility. The course is taught through performance-based learning methods with emphasis on drafting.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - F, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: LAW
title: Property
description: An examination of the fundamental concepts of property law and the types of property interests recognized by Anglo-Canadian law. course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - F, Fee Rate Group(International) -D, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: LAW

description: An analysis and critique of the law of torts, primarily the law of negligence, with personal injury as the main focus, although other torts will also be introduced. The nature of tort law and its process; an anatomy of the law of negligence - the nature and extent of liability, defences, remedies, and the assessment of damages; intentional torts; economic torts; strict liability; bailment; the impact of private insurance on the tort system; alternative forms of compensation.

subject: LAW
title: Foundations in Law and Justice I

subject: LAW

subject: LAW

subject: LAW

It also introduces students to the checks which courts place on the exercise of administrative power. The course discusses the procedures that courts require of administrative agencies and public officials as well as the substantive grounds on which courts may review the decisions of administrative agencies and public officials.

subject: LAW
title: Civil Procedure
description: A detailed examination of issues which arise in the progress of a civil action from first meeting the client through to judgment in the Alberta Court of Queen's Bench. The Alberta Rules of Court are set in the context of the values underlying them. What sort of civil litigation system do we want? What sort of system do we in fact have? Particular attention if paid to the linkages between the apparently discrete components of the process as set out in the Rules, linkages at the levels of both the underlying values and of actual practice. The use of procedures under the Rules to anticipate and resolve evidence problems that might arise at trial is stressed. Interprovincial and international aspect of the civil litigation process are also considered.

subject: LING

subject: LWFT
title: Contracts
description: A legal and policy analysis of the basic principles and fundamental concepts of the law of contracts as they relate to commercial and consumer transactions. The formation of contracts including offer and acceptance, and consideration; estoppel; privity; terms of contract, including exemption clauses; standard form contracts; bailment; mistake, misrepresentation and unconscionability; termination, including the doctrine of frustration; breach and remedies for breach; dispute resolution processes. Emphasis is placed not only on a knowledge of rules and principles, their historical derivation, rationale, efficacy and social validity, but also upon their creative use to both avoid and resolve disputes.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -F, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: LWFT
title: Property
description: An examination of the fundamental concepts of property law and the types of property interests recognized by Anglo-Canadian law. The historical evolution of property concepts; the basic concepts of possession, ownership and title; estates and other interests in land such as joint and concurrent ownership, easements, covenants, licences, mortgages, future interests and perpetuities; the landlord and tenant relationship; the land titles system of registration of title to land; the social constraints upon property use and disposition; and property rights of aboriginal peoples.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -F, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: LWFT
title: Torts
description: An analysis and critique of the law of torts, primarily the law of negligence, with personal injury as the main focus, although other torts will also be introduced. The nature of tort law and its process; an anatomy of the law of negligence - the nature and extent of liability, defences, remedies, and the assessment of damages; intentional torts; economic torts; strict liability; bailment; the impact of private insurance on the tort system; alternative forms of compensation.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -F, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: LWFT
title: Civil Procedure
description: A detailed examination of issues which arise in the progress of a civil action from first meeting the client through to judgment in the Alberta Court of Queen's Bench. The Alberta Rules of Court are set in the context of the values underlying them. What sort of civil litigation system do we want? What sort of system do we in fact have? Particular attention if paid to the linkages between the apparently discrete components of the process as set out in the Rules, linkages at the levels of both the underlying values and of actual practice. The use of procedures under the Rules to anticipate and resolve evidence problems that might arise at trial is stressed. Interprovincial and international aspect of the civil litigation process are also considered.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -F, GFC Hours (3-0), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: LWFT
title: Evidence
description: An examination of the fundamental concept of evidence law, including the traditional rules as compared to the emerging principled approach, and such core and primary topics as: the adversary system; relevance and discretionary exclusion; privilege; burdens of proof; character evidence; judicial notice; competence and compellability; examination of witnesses; hearsay; opinion evidence.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -F, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: LWFT
title: Business Associations
description: The common forms of business organization, including the law of agency, partnerships, limited partnerships, and corporations, with a focus on the corporation and the rights and responsibilities of shareholders and directors. Topics will include fiduciary relationships in a commercial context.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -F, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: LWFT
title: Family Law
description: An analysis of the legal principles affecting the rights and responsibilities of the members of the family. Topics include constitutional issues, marriage, marriage contracts, common law marriage, child neglect and abuse, custody and access, guardianship, adoption, separation, divorce, nullity, spousal and child maintenance, and matrimonial property. Stress is placed on the process of family law and the appropriate role for lawyers and judges.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -F, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: LWFT
title: Basic Tax Law
description: The basic language and concepts of taxation and identification of taxation issues. Topics include the unit of taxation, the meaning and taxation of income, taxation of benefits, the type and scope of deductions available for business income, and the taxation of capital gains including gains (and losses) on taxpayer assets.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -F, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: LWFT
title: Remedies
description: Judicial remedies at common law and equity for tort and breach of contract, including personal injury and property damage. Themes include compensating loss, disgorging gain, and punishing civil wrong; prohibiting and compelling defendant behaviour; loss-based, gain-based, and punitive damages; and injunctions and specific performance.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - H, Fee Rate Group(International) -F, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: LWFT

Current legal developments (including decided Canadian cases) will be covered to illustrate how concepts such as risk, negligence, neighbour principle, contractual obligations, offer and acceptance, consideration, remedies and punishment play out in contemporary Canadian society.

All anatomy and clinical skills related to the topics covered will be included.

subject: MDCN
title: Clerkship Electives
description:
During these mandatory 16 weeks of clerkship, clerks will choose electives from the range of potential medical domains. Sixteen weeks of mandatory elective time must be completed during the clerkship year with a minimum of two weeks on any one elective block.

Clerks will spend one week each in Interprofessional Education (IPE) and Community Engaged Learning (CEL) electives. In IPE, students will spend time with one or more allied health professionals to better understand the role that these individuals play in the multidisciplinary health care system. In CEL, students will be exposed to community partner organizations that serve disadvantaged groups in society. Students will be exposed to concepts in didactic sessions related to health care inequality and social disadvantage; students will then complete time working with a partner organization to see how these factors affect community members.
