Students learn to develop diagnostic plans and understand principles of laboratory diagnostic testing. Implementation of intervention measures for viral and prion infections and diseases are discussed.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Bacteriology
description: Introduction to fundamental principles of bacteriology, and bacterial diseases of domestic animals. Provides an understanding of how bacteria interact with the environment and the animal host, and how bacterial virulence mechanisms lead to animal diseases. Diagnosis of bacterial infections, and matching of appropriate preventive and control measures with different pathogens are discussed.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Parasitology
description: Introduction to fundamental principles of parasitism in domestic and wild animals. Emphasis is placed on understanding the occurrence, transmission and impacts of parasites, and diagnosis of parasitic diseases of clinical, trade, and zoonotic importance in North America.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Systemic Pathology
description: Using a species-specific approach to review common disease conditions. Students identify and describe common gross and microscopic lesions and formulate a morphologic diagnosis. Disease pathogenesis, tissue sampling, sample submission, and the value of ancillary diagnostic testing, and communicating post-mortem findings are emphasized.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: One Health and Veterinary Practice
description: Students will use a One Health approach to explore key issues at the interface of humans, animals and the environment. Students will integrate information, apply critical thinking skills to manage risks and develop prevention and control strategies for zoonoses and antimicrobial resistance; enhance food production, food safety and animal welfare; and protect the environment.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (33 hours)

subject: VETM
title: Clinical Pathology
description: Students develop a systematic approach to the use, evaluation and correct interpretation of routine clinical pathology tests. Integration of laboratory results with the patient's clinical presentation is emphasized. Correct interpretation of routine laboratory tests, communication of results, and appropriate integration of lab tests into decision-making in daily practice are covered.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Clinical Pharmacology and Toxicology
description: Effective and safe use of drugs in veterinary medicine. Basic principles of pharmacology, including mechanisms of action, for the major drug classes. Clinical toxicology principles that apply to common poisonings and adverse drug reactions.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Diagnostic Imaging
description: Introduction to principles and uses of common diagnostic imaging modalities. The theoretical basis behind each imaging technology, the acquisition of quality images, and the ability to interpret and describe normal and abnormal findings are emphasized. Control measures for working safely with diagnostic imaging equipment are examined.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (33 hours)

subject: VETM
title: Outbreak Investigation
description: Building on Veterinary Medicine 420, students further develop the framework for investigating outbreaks of disease. Students investigate a series of simulated outbreaks, applying steps to determine whether an outbreak exists, establishing a case definition, describing the epidemiology of the disease, generating and testing hypotheses, and communicating their findings.
prerequisites_raw: Admission to the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) Program.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (27 HOURS)

subject: VETM
title: Foreign Animal Disease
description: Students work through a simulation of an incursion of foreign animal disease into Canada. The simulation and background gives students experience working with disease surveillance, case identification, emergency preparedness, and the role of public practice veterinarians in maintaining the safety of Canadian livestock.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (27 HOURS)

subject: VETM
title: Career Options and Field Experiences in Veterinary Medicine
description: Students are exposed to career options in clinical and non-clinical veterinary medicine.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (27 Hours)

subject: VETM
title: Applied Nutrition
description: Core concepts pertaining to nutritional requirements, feeding regimes, and nutritional disorders in production and companion animals are examined. Feeding management of exotic animals is also discussed. Emphasis is placed on practical application of nutritional concepts in production and companion animals.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (33 hours)

subject: VETM
title: Clinical Presentations III
description: Building on Veterinary Medicine 300 and 400, students continue their development of diagnostic reasoning skills and problem management in veterinary medicine. Students synthesize comprehensive treatment plans that take into account therapeutic approaches, outcomes, feasibility, economics, client expectations, compliance, public health, regulations, and the environment.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Clinical Skills III
description: Building on Veterinary Medicine 305 and 405, students gain experience in clinical evaluations, routine anaesthesia and surgery. Diagnostic and therapeutic skills, practical clinical intervention, case management, and disease prevention knowledge and skills are further developed.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (0-6)

subject: VETM
title: Investigative Veterinary Medicine and Science Communication
description: Building on first and second year training in investigative medicine, students will have the opportunity to answer a real-world veterinary question while working under the guidance of faculty mentors. Based on their interests, students will choose from conducting a literature review on a controversial topic in veterinary medicine, analysis and preparation of existing data for publication, or preparation/planning for participation in a fourth year Investigative Medicine rotation. Principles and application of evidence-based medicine, critical thinking and effective communication of science to stakeholder groups will be emphasized.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (1.5-1.5), Research & Creative Scholarship - Focused

subject: VETM
title: Professional Skills III
description: Building on Veterinary Medicine 307 and 407, students will develop professional skills necessary for dealing with challenging issues in veterinary medicine. The concept of the healthy veterinarian and self-management will be expanded.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (1.5-1.5), WIL Service Learning

subject: VETM
title: Equine Medicine and Surgery
description: Prepares students for general equine practice by providing the foundational knowledge needed for diagnosing and treating  common equine diseases using medical or surgical approaches. Emphasizes the importance of professional conduct in the context of equine practice and promotes life-long continuing education.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Small Animal Medicine and Surgery
description: Prepares students for small animal practice by providing the foundational knowledge needed for diagnosing and treating common diseases in cats and dogs using medical or surgical approaches. Promotes practices that comply with animal welfare professional conduct.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Anesthesiology and Therapeutics
description: Introduction to the principals and practice of veterinary anaesthesiology and therapeutics in production, companion and exotic animals, and the practical application of clinical pharmacology. Focus on local and general anaesthesia for low risk animals and on therapeutic decisions, drug selection, and drug delivery.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Advanced Health Management
description: Provides an overview of diagnosing, managing, and preventing common disorders that occur at a population level. Emphasis is placed upon application of evidence-based medicine to make a herd diagnosis and control, and prevent the problem. Health programs and animal welfare assessment for production and companion animals are explored.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Selected Topics in Clinical Medicine
description: Prepares students for clinical practice by providing the foundational knowledge needed for diagnosing and treating oncologic, ophthalmic and dermatological diseases in production and companion animals.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Sel Topics Small Ruminant, South American Camelid & Non-trad Livestock Prod
description: Selected medical, surgical and reproductive diseases of small ruminants, South American camelids and non-traditional livestock.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Food Animal Medicine and Surgery
description: Prepares students for general food animal practice by providing the foundational knowledge needed for diagnosing, treating and preventing common diseases using medical or surgical approaches. Promotes practices that comply with animal welfare and professional conduct.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Theriogenology
description: Provides knowledge and skills to develop clinical competence in managing the reproductive health of production and companion animals. Students integrate knowledge from various disciplines to diagnose and manage clinical issues pertaining to the reproductive health of animals on an individual animal or herd basis.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Emergency and Critical Care
description: Veterinary emergency and critical care, with emphasis on how to recognize and implement therapy in the unstable patient.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Zoological Medicine
description: Provides the foundational knowledge needed for diagnosing, treating and preventing common diseases in non-traditional companion animal and wildlife species.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Laboratory Animal Medicine
description: Provides an introduction to laboratory animal medicine and disease, roles of the laboratory animal veterinarian and animal care committees, and the involvement of animals in research and teaching.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Veterinary Diagnostics and Therapeutics
description: Required for entering general veterinary practice. Students must successfully complete rotations in laboratory diagnostics, pathology, diagnostic imaging and other disciplines.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (4-8 wks), WIL Mandatory Clinical Placement

subject: VETM
title: General Veterinary Practice
description: Required for entering general veterinary practice. Students must successfully complete clinical rotations in general veterinary practice at various sites.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (12 Weeks), WIL Mandatory Clinical Placement

subject: VETM
title: Clinical Enrichment
description: Students choose elective rotations from a range of practicum experiences in veterinary medicine in order to expand or deepen their knowledge and skills.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (18-24 wks), WIL Mandatory Clinical Placement

subject: VETM
title: Professional Skills in Health Science Research
description: Includes a series of workshops focusing on skills essential for success in health science research. Topics include: Research Integrity; Ethics; Grants and Grant Writing; Verbal and Written Communication of Research Findings; Career Development; and Career Options in the Health Sciences.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0), Entrepreneurial Thinking - Related

subject: VETM
title: Wildlife Health and Disease Ecology
description: Ecological, epidemiological, and evolutionary principles needed to understand the determinants of health and diseases on wildlife populations, and their link to global changes, agriculture, public health, and conservation. Fundamental concepts in epidemiology and disease ecology will be presented as well as contemporary emerging issues in disease ecology. Using `case studies', lectures, discussions, examples, and activities, material will cover the etiology, pathology, and impact of a wide variety of wildlife diseases. The course will also cover the principles underlying a shift from disease-centered to health-centered approaches, and concepts of wildlife health ecology and management will be explored.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Experiential Learning in Wildlife Health Ecology
description: Experiential learning or research experience tailored to the unique goals or career path of the student. Involvement with the Distributed Wildlife Learning Community (DWLC) to broaden, extend, and deepen learning by integrating wildlife health ecology theory with practical application of knowledge.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (140 HOURS), WIL Internship

subject: VETM
title: (MDCH605)Intro Biostat Methods
description: Analysis and design of research related to biological sciences. Emphasis is placed upon formulating good research questions, evaluating the appropriateness of different statistical methods for analyzing results, and performing and interpreting such statistical analyses. Statistical analyses will be carried out using modern statistical software.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-1T)

subject: VETM
title: Seminar in Wildlife Health and Ecology I
description: Exposure to a variety of Wildlife Health Ecology (WHE) research topics, projects, and activities. Students will develop their presentation skills by presenting on their research and expanding their critical thinking through discussions of WHE topics presented at seminars or research meetings.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (1.5S-0)

subject: VETM
title: Seminar in Wildlife Health and Ecology II
description: Exposure to a variety of Wildlife Health Ecology (WHE) research topics, projects, and activities. Students will develop their presentation skills by presenting on their research and expanding their critical thinking through discussions of WHE topics presented at seminars or research meetings.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (1.5S-0)

subject: VETM
title: (MDCH610)Biostatistics I: Essentials of Biostatistics
description: Introduces the fundamental concepts of summarizing data and statistical inference, including graphical displays, hypothesis testing, p-values, and confidence intervals. Specific topics include comparisons of means and proportions, non-parametric tests, correlation and regression, confounding, sample size determination, and power calculations. Additional topics include a brief introduction to analysis of variance and covariance, logistic regression, and analysis of time-to-event data. Students gain hands-on experience analysing data using STATA statistical software. Although this course uses STATA exclusively, much of the technical knowledge and some of the computing techniques are applicable to any statistical package.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-2T)

subject: VETM
title: (MDCH611)Biostatistics II: Models for Health Outcomes
description: Extends the fundamental concepts to modelling health outcomes using modern regression analysis techniques. Logistic and linear regressions, and their extensions, are covered in detail. The rationale, formulation, and statistical assumptions underlying each regression technique are discussed. Methods for selecting and assessing models are included. Additional topics include a brief introduction to models used in the analysis of repeated measures, longitudinal studies, and time-to-event data.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-2T)

subject: VETM
title: Animal Health Policy
description: Develop student's ability to apply principles of quantitative analysis and policy to guided analysis of production animal health policy as well as development of a research project proposal in animal health policy. The proposal will include: formulation of hypothesis and testable policy research questions; consideration of policy research methods; basic experimental design incorporating appropriate (e.g., epidemiology, economic) analysis; and outline for policy analysis of results.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: (MDCH640)Fundamentals of Epidemiology
description: Principles and methods of descriptive and analytic epidemiology. Emphasizes the underlying concepts and approaches of epidemiological research and critical appraisal of epidemiologic studies including: observational study designs and their vulnerabilities to bias, measures of frequency and association, basic methods for addressing sampling variability, confounding, and effect modification. Concepts related to causal judgment in epidemiology are also introduced.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-2T)

subject: VETM
title: Advanced Virology
description: A series of lectures and discussions about current topics in virology. The lectures will be delivered by researchers working on aspects of molecular virology, virus-host interactions, and clinical virology, both from the veterinary and human field. One theme will be discussed during each session and students are expected to prepare presentations about virological topics and participate in the critical evaluation of journal articles.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3/2-0)

subject: VETM
title: Molecular Epidemiology and Evolution
description: Introduction to the evaluation of sequence data of bacteria, parasites, and viruses. Students will obtain background knowledge on the evolution of pathogens, the generation of sequence data, the evaluation of this data and directions for further study in this field. The course is a combination of lectures/workshops, self-study exercises, computer practices, and critical evaluation of research papers.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3/2-0)

subject: VETM
title: Directed Study
description: Lectures, seminars, term papers and/or other training directed to one or only a few students in theoretical and/or laboratory methods at the advanced level in veterinary medical sciences. These courses are offered when no other suitable alternatives are available.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Advanced Topics in Reproductive Health
description: A series of topics, ranging from basic sciences to clinical topics (including ethical issues) to increase awareness and comprehension regarding current issues in reproductive health.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Advanced Topics in Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine
description: Provides a comprehensive overview of stem cell biology in the context of embryonic development and adult tissue maintenance. Students will gain an appreciation for embryonic versus adult stem cells and how these pluripotent or multipotent cells may be utilized in regenerative medicine (i.e. treatment of congenital defects, diseases or injury).
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Experiential Learning in Veterinary Medical Sciences
description: Experiential learning or research experience tailored to the unique goals or career path of the student. Involvement with the Distributed Wildlife Learning Community (DWLC) to broaden, extend, and deepen learning by integrating wildlife health ecology theory with practical application of knowledge.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (140 HOURS), Research & Creative Scholarship - Related

subject: VETM
title: Seminar in Wildlife Health and Ecology III
description: Exposure to a variety of Wildlife Health Ecology (WHE) research topics, projects, and activities. Students will develop their presentation skills by presenting on their research and expanding their critical thinking through discussions of WHE topics presented at seminars or research meetings.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (1.5S-0)

subject: VETM
title: Seminar in Wildlife Health and Ecology IV
description: Exposure to a variety of Wildlife Health Ecology (WHE) research topics, projects, and activities. Students will develop their presentation skills by presenting on their research and expanding their critical thinking through discussions of WHE topics presented at seminars or research meetings.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (1.5S-0)

subject: VETM
title: Wildlife Parasitology: Principles and Techniques
description: Students will learn about the ecology of parasites in wildlife populations with emphasis on impacts of parasitism, invasive species, and conservation issues. This is taught through a series of seminars, critical evaluation and discussion of the literature, and independent and group projects. Laboratory sessions include on parasitology techniques for surveillance and research.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-0)

subject: VETM
title: Advanced Epidemiology
description: An expansion on the understanding of causality and threats to validity in epidemiologic research. The focus will be on the assessment and control of bias, including selection, information and confounding. The concept of effect modification (interaction) will be appraised. Stratified analysis will be considered as a tool for the assessment and control of confounding and effect modification and will be applied to a variety of study designs including case-control, and cohort studies.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -B, GFC Hours (3-2T)

subject: VTMD
title: Introduction to Veterinary Medicine
description: An introduction to the veterinary medicine program. A primer for the safe handling of multispecies animals and a basic overview of the breadth of the veterinary profession.
prerequisites_raw: Admission to the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) Program.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (28 HOURS)

subject: VTMD
title: Professional Identity Formation I
description: Explores the basic skills fundamental to a successful career in veterinary medicine. Topics will include leadership of self, working effectively in teams, ethics, role of research in veterinary medicine, veterinary informatics, new technology, introduction to financial concepts, and professional communication
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (1-3-2T)

subject: VTMD
title: Exploring Veterinary Medicine I
description: Introduces key skills and knowledge including basic surgical principles, biosecurity, husbandry, normal animal behaviour, and general animal handling and restraint.
prerequisites_raw: Admission to the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) Program.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (1.5-1.5T-3)

subject: VTMD
title: Healthy Animals I
description: The basics of nomenclature, anatomy, physiology, clinical skills, clinical presentations, and diagnostic imaging for normal, healthy animals. Modules cover integument, musculoskeletal, neurology, respiratory, cardiovascular, and lymphatic systems.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (4-6-4T)

subject: VTMD
title: Practical Work Experience I
description: Students spend a week in a veterinary work setting allowing students to dive deeper into regulatory and industry, research, clinical practice, or food production.
prerequisites_raw: Admission to the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) Program.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (28 HOURS), WIL Mandatory Clinical Placement

subject: VTMD
title: Animals As Populations
description: More basic universal skills that are fundamental to success as a veterinarian. Covers nutrition, foundations of population health, epidemiology, and the basics of health management.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(International) -A, Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, GFC Hours

subject: VTMD
title: What Is A Veterinarian
description: An exploration of what it means to be a veterinarian. The scope of practice, the value of the profession, and a veterinarian's role in contributing to the health and well-being of society, including One Health and animal welfare.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-1.5T)

subject: VTMD
title: Healthy Animals II
description: The nomenclature, anatomy, physiology, clinical skills, clinical presentations, and diagnostic imaging for normal, healthy animals. Modules cover the head, oral cavity, gastrointestinal system, endocrine system, urinary system, reproductive system, fetal, special senses, and alternative species.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (4-6-4T)

subject: VTMD
title: Professional Identity Formation II
description: Expands on communication skills and explores wellness concepts, including conflict management, resolution, and leadership skills. It also integrates interprofessional learning, including the integration into a team of health professionals and collaborative problem-solving.
prerequisites_raw: Admission to the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) Program and Veterinary Medicine 202.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-6-1.5T)

subject: VTMD
title: Science of What Goes Wrong I
description: Pathologic basis of disease, pharmacology, toxicology, and oncology. An introduction to the basic disease mechanisms, basics of pharmaco/ toxico-kinetics, basic mechanisms of action of pharmaceuticals, and the derangement of homeostasis.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (4-1.5-2T)

subject: VTMD
title: Science of What Goes Wrong II
description: Basic systemic pathology, bacteriology, virology, parasitology, and mycology. Organ reactions to infection, basic organ dysfunction, basics of host-pathogen interactions, and mechanisms of disease spread.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (4-1.5-2T)

subject: VTMD
title: Fundamentals of Diagnosis, Management and Treatment
description: Integrates relevant physiology, anatomy, pharmacology, anesthesiology, clinical pathology, anatomic pathology, and analgesia to explore reasons and methods for collecting and recording diagnostic information. Basic tenets of population management and individual treatment plans.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-1.5T-1.5)

subject: VTMD
title: Practical Work Experience II
description: Students spend a week in a veterinary work setting allowing a deeper dive into regulatory and industry, research, clinical practice, or food production.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (28 HOURS), WIL Mandatory Clinical Placement

subject: VTMD
title: Veterinarians in Society
description: An exploration of the veterinarian's role within the community and contribution to society. Includes the study of scientific communication, context-specific communication strategies, concepts of One Health, cultural humility, and Indigenous ways of knowing in the context of animal care and use.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours

subject: VTMD
title: Head, Oral, and Gastrointestinal
description: Integrates anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pathology of specific diseases, diagnostic imaging, surgery, medicine, immunology, analgesia, anesthesia, and epidemiology to explore pathologic alterations and the diagnosis and treatment of conditions related to the head, oral cavity, and gastrointestinal tract of sick animals.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2T-2)

subject: VTMD
title: Endocrine, Renal, and Reproduction
description: Integrates anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pathology of specific diseases (clinical and systemic), diagnostic imaging, surgery, medicine, immunology, analgesia, anesthesia, and epidemiology to explore pathologic alterations and the diagnosis and treatment of conditions related to the endocrine system, urinary system, reproductive system of sick animals..
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2T-2)

subject: VTMD
title: Neonatal, Special Senses, Alternative Species
description: Integrates anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pathology of specific diseases (clinical and systemic), diagnostic imaging, surgery, medicine, immunology, analgesia, anesthesia, and epidemiology to explore pathologic alterations and the diagnosis and treatment of conditions related to neonatal concerns, special senses and concerns of alternative species.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2T-2)

subject: VTMD
title: Group Problem-Solving
description: Students work in small groups to solve clinical cases based on a presenting complaint. In addition to honing their clinical reasoning skills, students will also participate in laboratories to improve communication skills. Student groups will also be responsible for presenting cases to Year 1 students.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (2-4T)

subject: VTMD
title: Introduction to Clinical Rotations
description: Bridges the school experience and the clinical experience. Students participate in faculty-led clinical rotations in diagnostic, small, and large animal facilities. Topics one week each: Fundamentals in medicine, Fundamentals in Surgery, Fundamentals in Anatomic Pathology, Fundamentals in Clinical Pathology, Fundamentals in diagnostic imaging, Fundamentals in anesthesia, Fundamentals in preventative and population medicine, Fundamentals in Diagnostic Imaging.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (196 Hours)

subject: VTMD
title: Topics in Veterinary Medicine
description: An opportunity to explore veterinary medicine topics of interest in more detail. Topics available will vary from year-to-year.
prerequisites_raw: Admission to the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) Program and Veterinary Medicine 420, 422, 424.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (18 HOURS)

subject: VTMD
title: Integument and Musculoskeletal
description: Integrates anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pathology of specific diseases (clinical and systemic), diagnostic imaging, surgery, medicine, immunology, analgesia, anesthesia, and epidemiology to explore pathologic alterations and the diagnosis and treatment of conditions related to the integumentary and musculoskeletal systems of sick animals.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2T-2)

subject: VTMD
title: Neurology and Respiratory
description: Integrates anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pathology of specific diseases (clinical and systemic), diagnostic imaging, surgery, medicine, immunology, analgesia, anesthesia, and epidemiology to explore pathologic alterations and the diagnosis and treatment of conditions related to the neurology and respiratory systems of sick animals.
course_attributes: Fee Rate Group(Domestic) - A, Fee Rate Group(International) -A, GFC Hours (3-2T-2)

subject: VTMD
title: Cardiovascular and Lymphatic
description: Integrates anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pathology of specific diseases (clinical and systemic), diagnostic imaging, surgery, medicine, immunology, analgesia, anesthesia, and epidemiology to explore pathologic alterations and the diagnosis and treatment of conditions related to the cardiovascular and lymphatic systems of sick animals.

subject: VTMD
title: Introduction to Surgery, Anesthesia, and Hospitalized Case Management
description: Begins with relevant anesthesia and surgery lectures and then allows students to take primary case responsibility for basic surgical sterilization procedures in healthy small animals. Covers admission of the patient through to assessment, surgical, anesthetic, analgesic, and post-operative care and discharge back to the guardian of the animal. Develop accurate and acceptable medical records and practice functioning as part of an integrated medical team.
prerequisites_raw: Admission to the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) Program and Veterinary Medicine 304 and 306.

subject: ZOOL
title: An Introduction to Invertebrate Zoology
description: Natural history and diversity of invertebrates, which include sponges, corals, jellyfish, snails, octopus, insects, crustaceans, sea stars, and various worms. Emphasis on how free-living and parasitic organisms feed, move, reproduce, and survive in marine, freshwater, and terrestrial habitats.

subject: ZOOL
title: An Introduction to Vertebrate Zoology
description: Systematics, natural history and biology of vertebrates, including fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals. Laboratory work will emphasize the identification and morphology of native taxa as well as basic techniques of biological systematics.

subject: ZOOL

subject: ZOOL
title: Animal Physiology II
description: Study of body fluids and hemostasis, body defence systems, reproductive physiology, renal physiology, respiration, circulation, excretion, gastrointestinal physiology and thermoregulation.

subject: ZOOL
